confirmed.title: Self-check treats a stale status as 'Recorder running', so a dead recorder can pass and the update auto-rollback never fires
confirmed.description: run_checks() unpacks (doc, problem) from read_status but only fails 'Recorder running' when doc is None. read_status returns the old document plus a problem string when the heartbeat is stale, and run_checks throws the problem away. I checked it: a status.json one hour old saying RECORDING/connected gives 'Everything works.', and the check then marks those settings as known good. A stale STOPPED document gives 'Recorder running: True' and 'Recorder state: False'. window._update_watch_failed (window.py:828) goes back to the previous version automatically only if 'Settings file' or 'Recorder running' failed. That never happens when the old version's shutdown left a STOPPED status, which is exactly the case after an update.
confirmed.failure_scenario: After an update, the new version's recorder service does not come back (crash at start, SCM retrying) and status.json still holds the old version's final STOPPED document. The 3-minute watch fails only on 'Recorder state'. broken is empty, so instead of going back to the previous version the window says the problem 'is usually not caused by the update (camera, drive)'. Recording stays down. Separately, Check everything while the recorder is hung or killed reports 'Everything works' and overwrites the known-good settings.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In run_checks, when problem is not None (stale), add Check('Recorder running', False, problem) and return. Or pass the ReadKind from read_status_robust so a stale or future heartbeat fails.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this one, and I reproduced it. In src/sentinel/selfcheck.py, lines 80-84 fail "Recorder running" only when doc is None. sentinel.status.read_status (status.py:265-267) returns the old document together with an X-001 problem string when the heartbeat is stale. run_checks throws that string away and marks "Recorder running" True.

A clean stop leaves a stale document. evaluate() with stopping=True (status.py:70-71) gives overall STOPPED with no alerts, and service.py:309 writes it with terminal=False. The update stops the recorder gracefully, so after an update status.json holds exactly that document. In update mode, window._update_watch_failed (window.py:828) goes back to the previous version automatically only when "Settings file" or "Recorder running" failed. With a stale STOPPED document only "Recorder state" fails, so the set is empty. The window then shows "This is usually not caused by the update (camera, drive)" and does not go back.

Nothing earlier catches this. cmd_finish -> start_recording (apply.py:293-299) only checks the return code of `sc start`, which returns once the start request is accepted. A recorder that hangs during startup or recovery, or dies without writing status, passes finish. The window's 3-minute watch is the only safety net, and this bug disables it.

The second scenario also holds. A status one hour old saying RECORDING/connected gives "Everything works." with the default require_saved_file=True, because the last file is still within its due window. With require_saved_file=False, which is what the watch uses, it always passes. check_now (window.py:641-643) then saves those settings as known good.

Why I put it at medium, not high:
- Many startup failures do not reach this path. winsvc/__main__.py:_startup_failure and service.py:216-218 write a fresh terminal C-001 status, so the heartbeat is not stale.
- The stale case needs a defective update whose recorder hangs, crashes hard, or starts slowly, without writing any status.
- The dashboard uses read_status_robust and still shows X-001.
- The agent can still go back by hand under System > Updates.
- Settings-change mode is not affected: it rolls back on any failure, and a stale STOPPED document already fails "Recorder state".

So this is a real defeat of the update auto-rollback plus a misleading "Everything works" message, with a manual workaround. The suggested fix is right: when problem is not None, add Check("Recorder running", False, problem) and return. Alternatively, use read_status_robust and fail when kind is not ReadKind.OK.

confirmed.title: 'Cancel swap' stays hidden for a drive awaiting return, while the status message tells the agent to press it
confirmed.description: swap_under_way() (uncommitted change) checks arc.get('awaiting_return'). arc is the recorder's archive view (RecorderArchiveView.evaluate, archive/status.py:219-221), which copies only running/state/drive/message/backlog/drive_label/drives/removal. 'awaiting_return' never reaches status.json, so this check is always false. The worker's new _awaiting_text() message says 'To keep using it without an office copy, press Cancel swap.' I checked it: the view keys have no awaiting_return, and swap_under_way(view) is False with an awaiting drive inserted.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A drive taken out with Swap is plugged back in without an office copy (state ABSENT or COPYING to the other drive, removal None). The Drives page and status text tell the agent to press Cancel swap, but the button is not shown. The drive is never written again until a Return to service, which needs a real office copy. The agent is stuck.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use the drives list that is already passed through: any(d.get('use') == 'awaiting_return' for d in arc.get('drives') or []). Or add 'awaiting_return' to the RecorderArchiveView output.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The bug is real.

1. The Drives page gets `arc` from the recorder's status.json, not from the copier's own status file. drive_pages.py:295 reads `read.doc["archive"]`, and service.py:763 fills that field from `RecorderArchiveView.evaluate`.
2. `RecorderArchiveView.evaluate` (archive/status.py:219-221) copies only these keys: running, state, drive, message, backlog, drive_label, drives and removal. The worker does write `awaiting_return` to its own file (worker.py:1513), but `evaluate` drops it. So the check `arc.get("awaiting_return")` in `swap_under_way` (drive_pages.py:64) is always false.
3. The other two checks in `swap_under_way` cannot catch this case either. Once the swapped drive has been taken out, `_swapped_drive` is cleared (worker.py:~350), so `removal` is None. The state is ABSENT, or COPYING to the other drive, and neither is one of the swap states.
4. The Drives page is the only place in the GUI with a Cancel swap button (`resume_btn`). The only other way to cancel is the admin command line (`archive resume`), which the non-technical agent will not use.
5. The button would work if it were shown. The resume handler calls `_set_awaiting(None)` (worker.py:243), which clears the waiting state.
6. The page still tells the agent to press the button. When the state is not ABSENT, the worker's `_awaiting_text` (worker.py:979-981) says "To keep using it without an office copy, press Cancel swap". docs/10_OFFICE_TRANSFER.md:53 also tells the agent to press Cancel swap.

Result: the agent is told to press a button that is not there, and the drive is never written to again until it goes through Return to service, which needs a real office copy. Recordings are not lost: they stay on the internal SSD, and another inserted drive keeps being copied to. With only one drive, the backlog grows until A-004 fires. That makes this medium: a misleading message plus a stuck agent, with a workaround (an office copy then Return to service, or an admin running `archive resume`). It falls short of critical.

Fix (either one):
- In `swap_under_way`, check the drives list that already reaches the page: `any(isinstance(d, dict) and d.get("use") == "awaiting_return" for d in arc.get("drives") or [])`.
- Or add `"awaiting_return": doc.get("awaiting_return")` to the view built in archive/status.py:219-221.

raw read: True
['backlog', 'drive', 'drive_label', 'drives', 'message', 'removal', 'running', 'state']
swap_under_way: False

confirmed.title: Schedule page silently rewrites valid config times and dates when saved (a holiday period can become 'pause from now')
confirmed.description: The config parser accepts 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM', a one-digit hour, seconds, and '24:00' as an end (schedule.py:70-71). parse_date_value only accepts 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm' and otherwise returns QDateTime.currentDateTime(). TimeCombo.set_value maps anything with seconds ('07:30:00') to 00:00 (normal_time has no seconds). A typed invalid time ('7:3', '25:00') makes value() return the previously selected list item. I checked all of these: '2026-12-24T18:00', '2026-12-24 8:00' and '2026-12-24 24:00' all load as 'now'. Weekly '07:30:00' loads as 00:00 (start) or 24:00 (end). Typed '25:00' saves 07:00.
confirmed.failure_scenario: [[schedule.dates]] in the file has action='pause', start='2026-12-24T00:00', end='2026-12-27' (valid, written by hand or in Notepad). An administrator opens Schedule and only changes the default action, then saves. The period is rewritten as pause from now until 28 Dec, and recording stops at once for six weeks. A weekly '07:00:00'-'18:00:00' record period becomes all day.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Parse with the schedule module's own _DATE/_TIME regexes, including T, seconds, one-digit hour and 24:00. If a value cannot be represented, refuse to load the page for editing (show the raw text and a message) rather than substituting now/00:00. In TimeCombo.value(), raise a validation error for unparseable typed text instead of falling back to currentData().

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. When the Schedule page loads, it runs every period through parsers that are stricter than the recorder's own parser (schedule.py:70-71, _seconds/_datetime). When the page cannot read a value, it puts in "now" or 00:00 without saying so, and Save writes that back.

How it happens:
- ScheduleSettingsPage.load (settings_pages.py:751-753) passes each [[schedule.dates]] start and end to parse_date_value (settings_pages.py:510-520).
- For any value longer than 10 characters, parse_date_value only tries QDateTime.fromString(text[:16], "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"). If that fails, it returns QDateTime.currentDateTime().
- So '2026-12-24T00:00', '2026-12-24 8:00' and '2026-12-24 24:00' all load as the current time, even though parse_schedule accepts all three.
- Weekly times go through TimeCombo.set_value (settings_pages.py:448-458). normal_time (_TIME_RE) does not accept seconds, so '07:00:00' becomes 00:00.
- An end of '18:00:00' also becomes '00:00'. That is not an item in the end list, so value() maps it to 24:00. A 07:00:00-18:00:00 period becomes all day.
- Save then writes the result of tables(), so the changes are written to the config file.

Nothing guards against it. There is no comparison with the original, no confirmation, and no check that a value survived the load. The 14-day preview and the table do show the new times, but no message points to the change. A non-technical administrator who only changes the default action would very likely not notice that a December holiday pause now starts today.

What limits it:
- The GUI writes 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm' and HH:MM. The shipped example config/sentinel.example.toml uses the same forms.
- So it only happens when someone typed a non-standard but valid value into the file by hand, and then saved the Schedule page from the window.
- Unquoted TOML datetimes are not a second way in: parse_schedule rejects them because they are not strings.

I kept the severity at medium. It is wrong behaviour that silently stops recording until the period's end. But it needs a hand-edited, non-standard config plus a later GUI save, and the preview shows the result.

The suggested fix is right. Parse with schedule._DATE and schedule._TIME (accepting T, seconds, a one-digit hour and 24:00 as an end). If a value cannot be shown in the widgets, refuse to edit and display the raw text instead of putting in now or 00:00.
verdict.evidence:
I read src/sentinel/gui/app/settings_pages.py lines 415-520 (normal_time, TimeCombo.set_value/value, parse_date_value) and 744-780 (load/tables), and src/sentinel/schedule.py lines 70-71 and 118-145 (_TIME/_DATE, _seconds, _datetime). I ran a throwaway script outside the repo with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen and PYTHONPATH=src:
2026-12-24T00:00 -> 2026-11-12 23:45 (start), 2026-11-12 23:45 (end)
2026-12-24 8:00 -> 2026-11-12 23:45
2026-12-24 24:00 -> 2026-11-12 23:45
2026-12-24 18:00 -> 2026-12-24 18:00 (correct)
parse_schedule accepts {'start':'2026-12-24T00:00','end':'2026-12-27'} as pause 2026-12-24 00:00 to 2026-12-28 00:00, and also accepts weekly 07:00:00-18:00:00.
TimeCombo().set_value('07:00:00').value() -> '00:00'; TimeCombo(end=True).set_value('18:00:00').value() -> '24:00'.
The shipped config/sentinel.example.toml uses only the standard '2026-12-24 18:00' form, so it takes a hand-edited config to trigger this.

confirmed.title: Recordings timeline shows the hour being recorded now as 'no information — reason not recorded'
confirmed.description: RecordingsPage calls load_timeline() with the default live_slack_s=600. Since 0.3.x segments are 3600 s by default (config.py:62), and the GUI reads the ledger snapshot, which is refreshed only every 5 min. The tail since the last sealed segment is usually more than 10 minutes, so build_timeline marks it NO_INFO with UNKNOWN_REASON instead of LIVE. I checked it: with 1-hour segments and the last seal 25 min ago, the result is 'no_info 25 min reason not recorded'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: For about 50 minutes of every hour, the agent or a reviewer looking at Recordings sees the current period hatched grey, with 'no information / reason not recorded' at the top of the table while the recorder is recording normally. This invites false incident reports or doubt about the evidence timeline.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass live_slack_s = cfg.recording.segment_seconds * 1.5 + snapshot interval (300 s) + margin. Also consider using status.last_segment/open_gap for the tail.

verdict.reasoning: I could not refute this. RecordingsPage.on_show (src/sentinel/gui/app/status_pages.py:478) calls load_timeline without passing live_slack_s, so it gets the default of 600 s (src/sentinel/gui/ledger_view.py:296). The default segment length is 3600 s (config.py:62), and both example configs set 3600. A segment row is only written to the ledger when the segment is sealed (finalizer.py:215, db.py:751). load_timeline also only selects rows where end_utc IS NOT NULL. So the time since the last seal is not covered by any row. It can be up to about 60 minutes, plus up to 5 minutes of snapshot lag (LEDGER_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_S = 300, service.py:80) when the window reads the snapshot. When there is no open gap, build_timeline (ledger_view.py:265) only labels the tail LIVE if it is 600 s or shorter. Otherwise it falls through to NO_INFO with UNKNOWN_REASON and ongoing=True (line 270). The live flag is set correctly when the dashboard reports a recording state, so the only cause is the slack value. For roughly 50 to 55 minutes of every hour of normal recording, the newest row in the table reads 'no information / reason not recorded / now', and the bar shows that span as grey dots. NO_INFO does not count as an interruption, so the summary still says 'not recorded 0 s in 0 gap(s)'. That contradicts the table, which makes it more confusing, but it also means no false gap count is produced. No recordings are affected; this is a misleading display only, so medium is the right severity. Fix: in on_show, pass live_slack_s=cfg.recording.segment_seconds*1.5 + LEDGER_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_S + about 60 s. Optionally, also take the tail from the status's last-sealed time or open gap.
verdict.evidence: Code read: status_pages.py:474-478 (load_timeline called without live_slack_s); ledger_view.py:265-271 (the tail becomes LIVE only when b-a <= live_slack_s, otherwise NO_INFO/UNKNOWN_REASON), :295-305 (default 600.0, segments with end_utc NOT NULL only); config.py:62 (segment_seconds=3600.0); service.py:80 (snapshot interval 300 s). Reproduced with build_timeline, using five sealed 1-hour segments, the last seal 25 min ago, live=True and slack 600. Output: 'no_info 2100 no record of the system running False / recorded 18000 / no_info 1500 reason not recorded True'. missing_s=0, interruptions=0.

confirmed.title: Status page shows the stale document's camera 'connected' (green) and old alerts as current when the recorder is not responding
confirmed.description: build_dashboard deliberately drops alerts and the camera state from a stale document ('Alerts inside a stale document are no longer current and are not shown'; camera tile 'Unknown'). StatusPage.on_status still iterates doc['alerts'] after adding X-001. _facts and _header still show camera_link, archive and storage from the stale doc with ok/green tones. I checked it: with a 10-minute-old status, the facts show 'connected' / 'connected' and the alerts show ['X-001', 'R-001'].
confirmed.failure_scenario: The recorder service crashes or hangs. The headline turns red, but the header and Details show 'Camera: connected' with a green tick, 'Connection: connected', and an old alert list as if live. The agent may report that the camera is fine and the recorder is OK.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When read.kind is not OK, show only X-001 (plus Z-001) in the alert tree, and show 'unknown' in neutral tone for the camera/link/archive facts (or label them 'last known').

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute it, and I reproduced it. AppWindow.refresh (window.py:388-412) passes the same StatusRead to build_dashboard and to StatusPage.on_status. A STALE read still carries the old document: read_status_robust returns StatusRead(doc, problem, STALE, age). build_dashboard drops the stale alerts on purpose (viewmodel.py:357, "Alerts inside a stale document are no longer current"). StatusPage.on_status (status_pages.py:279-286) adds X-001 and then still adds every alert in doc['alerts']. _header (status_pages.py:324-328) shows camera_link from the stale document with an "ok" tone. _facts (status_pages.py:374-375 for link, 388-389 for storage, 391-392 for archive with "ok" when running, 404-405 for clock) does the same with live-looking tones. Only the "Recorder" fact (413-416) and the "updated" header fact (362-363) check read.kind. Nothing else hides these values: on_status is called for every read and has no stale check besides X-001. The Status page is the first and home section, so this is what the agent sees.

The impact is limited. The headline still turns red ("System error"), X-001 is the first alert, "Recorder: not responding" is red, and the "updated" fact reads "not updating (X-001)". The agent does get a clear critical signal, but next to it is a green "Camera: connected", a green archive "running" and old alerts that look current. Over the phone that can lead the agent or support to wrongly report the camera, archive or copier as fine, and to chase an old alert. Nothing is lost or wedged, so this is medium, at the low end.

verdict.evidence:
I read status_pages.py lines 264-417, viewmodel.py lines 40-110 (read_status_robust keeps the doc on STALE) and 336-366 (build_dashboard's stale branch drops alerts), and window.py lines 388-412 (the same read goes to both). Output:
CODES ['X-001', 'R-001'] kind stale headline System error
LABEL ok 'connected'            (header camera fact, green)
LABEL critical 'not updating (X-001)'

confirmed.title: System › Restart recorder restarts with a configuration file that does not load, and does not start the check/rollback
confirmed.description: The Configuration file tab says: after editing in Notepad, 'use Restart recorder to apply them'. _reload_if_changed reports a broken file only in a 15-second status-bar message (and sets _cfg_mtime so it never repeats). restart_recorder/base.restart_recorder never re-validate the file on disk. They stop the service and start it, and the service then fails on the bad file (C-001). SystemPage._restart does not call watch_after_change, so the automatic return to the last working settings is not used. Depending on SCM timing, the result line can even say 'The recorder was restarted with the saved settings.' (ServiceControl.start returns ok once the service reaches RUNNING).
confirmed.failure_scenario: An administrator fixes a value in Notepad, leaves a typo, misses the 15-second note, and presses Restart recorder. The recording is stopped, the service loops on C-001 (shown as X-001, see the C-001 finding above), and nothing rolls back. If the window is later closed, the launcher cannot open it again because load_config fails, so the agent loses access to Settings history.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In restart_recorder, run load_config(path) first. If it fails, refuse with the error and offer Settings history / last known good. After a manual restart, also call watch_after_change().

verdict.reasoning:
The main defect holds up. The Configuration file tab (status_pages.py:669-671) tells the administrator to "use Restart recorder to apply" edits made in Notepad. Nothing on that path checks the file on disk first. window.restart_recorder (window.py:594-624) hands the in-memory ctx.cfg to base.restart_recorder (base.py:365-378). That function stops the running service (control.stop(90)) and then starts it again. The service host reloads the file (winsvc/__main__.py:522-526), gets a ConfigError and exits with EXIT_CONFIG. SCM recovery then retries every 60 s and fails each time. So pressing Restart turns a recorder that was working on the old settings into one that has stopped, and it stays stopped until someone repairs the file. _reload_if_changed (window.py:368-379) shows the parse error once, as a 15-second status-bar message, and sets _cfg_mtime so the message never comes back. ctx.cfg keeps the old valid settings, so the restart is not refused either. SystemPage._restart (status_pages.py:824-832) never calls watch_after_change, which means the automatic return to the last known good settings never runs. Compare the history-restore path (status_pages.py:767-768) and rollback_to_known_good (window.py:717-722), which both call it.

One sub-claim is wrong. The finding says the result can read "The recorder was restarted with the saved settings." It cannot, for a file that fails to load: ServiceHost.report_running() is only called after load_config succeeds (winsvc/__main__.py:558). The service goes from START_PENDING straight to STOPPED with service_exit_code=EXIT_CONFIG (scm.py:197-198), and ServiceControl.start (winsvc/control.py:102-105) returns C-001. The administrator therefore sees "The recorder could not be started (C-001). See System › Service." That message does not say the configuration file is broken and does not point to Check and history. The scenario needs an administrator who leaves a typo in Notepad, so the non-technical agent will not cause it in normal use, and a manual restore under System › Check and history fixes it. The broken file would also stop the recorder at the next reboot no matter what. The real harm is that the button stops a working recording on demand, gives a vague code, and does not roll back. That is wrong behaviour with a workaround, so medium. I did not verify the side claim that the launcher cannot reopen the window with a broken file (the console run path at launcher/cli.py:122-128 prints C-001 and exits). It is not needed for this finding.

Fix: in window.restart_recorder, or at the start of base.restart_recorder, call load_config(path) before stopping anything. If it fails, refuse with the error text and offer Settings history / last known good. After a manual restart, also call watch_after_change().
verdict.evidence:
Read the code (no runtime reproduction, because a real service would be needed):
- status_pages.py:669-671: "After editing it, Sentinel shows the new settings; use Restart recorder to apply them."
- window.py:373-379: _cfg_mtime = m is set before load_config, and on ConfigError there is only showMessage(..., 15000) and return. ctx.cfg stays the old valid config.
- window.py:602-608: cfg, path = self.ctx.cfg, self.ctx.cfg_path; Task(lambda: base.restart_recorder(path, cfg)). No validation of the file on disk.
- base.py:369-375: control.stop(90.0), then control.start(). A failure returns "The recorder could not be started ({code}). See System › Service."
- status_pages.py:824-832: _restart calls ctx.restart(on_done=done) only, with no after_change/watch_after_change. Compare status_pages.py:767-768 and window.py:717-722, which do call watch_after_change.
- winsvc/__main__.py:522-526: load_config(config) raises ConfigError, then _startup_failure(...) and return EXIT_CONFIG. host.report_running() is at line 558, after config loads, so SERVICE_RUNNING is never reported for a bad file.
- scm.py:197-198: STOPPED with service_exit=code. winsvc/control.py:102-105: STOPPED gives StartResult(False, "C-001"). This refutes the "restarted with the saved settings" sub-claim; the message shown is "could not be started (C-001)".

confirmed.title: Rename sends only the drive letter, with no identity check, so a replugged or relettered drive gets the new name
confirmed.description: _return passes --expect-uuid (fix 2026-11-12) and erase passes --fingerprint/--expect-class, but _rename passes only '--drive letters[0]' from a possibly stale list. drives rename (drives/cli.py:306-337, rename.py:82) renames whatever Sentinel drive is at that letter.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The list shows SSD_1 at E:. The agent swaps drives, and SSD_2 now has E:, without pressing Refresh. The agent selects the old 'SSD_1' row and renames it SSD_3. SSD_2 is renamed SSD_3 and the agent writes SSD_3 on SSD_1's sticker. The office transfer, Return to service and swap instructions then name the wrong physical drive.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the selected drive_uuid (add --expect-uuid to drives rename and refuse on mismatch), as is already done for Return to service.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism. DrivesPage._rename (drive_pages.py:487-510) takes the drive letter from the selected row of a list that may be out of date and runs `drives rename --drive <letter> --name --who`. It sends no drive_uuid or fingerprint. Neither cmd_rename (drives/cli.py:308-339) nor rename_drive (drives/rename.py:82-132) has any way to check the expected identity. rename_drive reads SENTINEL_DRIVE.json from whatever volume is at that root and renames it, provided the new name is not already taken.

The list really can be out of date. DriveList.refresh runs only when the page is shown (on_show), after Erase, Designate, Return, Rename or Eject finish, and when Refresh list is pressed. The window's periodic timer (window.py:101-103 / refresh at 388) re-reads only the status file and never refreshes the drive list. Swap runs from this same page through _arc (drive_pages.py:314-317), which has no on_done refresh. So after an agent swaps drives with the page open, rows still show the old letter-to-drive mapping. Windows often gives the new USB drive the same letter, or swaps letters between two drives that are re-inserted in a different order.

This is the same kind of guard that Return (--expect-uuid, line 481) and Erase (--fingerprint/--expect-class, lines 418-419) already have, and Rename lacks it. So the finding is real.

Why I put it at the low end of medium:
1. Nothing is lost. Rename only changes the volume label and the label in the marker. The drive keeps its drive_uuid, recordings and records, and the rename is written to the audit log with the drive_uuid.
2. It can be undone by renaming again.

confirmed.title: Automatic update rollback and the post-update watch both wait on a modal message box
confirmed.description: show_update_result() shows a modal QMessageBox and only after it is dismissed calls watch_after_change(mode='update'). The 3-minute recorder watch therefore does not start until a person clicks OK. In _update_watch_failed (line 832-834), the 'Sentinel now goes back to version …' warning is also modal and comes BEFORE tab.go_back(), so the automatic return to the previous version does not happen until someone clicks OK.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The agent applies an update and walks away while the finisher reopens the window. If nobody clicks the 'updated' box, nobody watches the recorder. If someone does, and the recorder then fails, the rollback sits behind a second dialog. The recorder stays down at an unattended remote site.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Start the watch before showing the result, and start go_back() before (or instead of) the modal warning. Use the status bar or a non-modal notice for information.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. The finding is real.

1. show_update_result (window.py:798-806) runs from QTimer.singleShot(500) at line 109. It marks the result shown=True. Then it calls the static, blocking QMessageBox.information/warning at line 803. watch_after_change(mode="update") at line 806 only runs after that call returns, so the 3-minute recorder watch does not start until someone dismisses the box.

2. _update_watch_failed (lines 819-835) calls _update_watch_done() first, which writes watch=False to last_update.json. Next it shows the blocking QMessageBox.warning at line 832 ("Sentinel now goes back to version ..."). tab.go_back(..., ask=False) at line 834 runs only after that. So the "automatic" rollback waits on a click.

Nothing else covers for this:
- The finisher's `update finish` only checks that the services start (`sc start` returns 0). The longer check that the recorder keeps running exists only in this window watch.
- The UpdatesTab help text (update_page.py:72-74) and the apply.py docstring (lines 20-22) both promise that it "goes back ... by itself" if the recorder does not work within 3 minutes.
- The existing test (tests/unit/test_gui_app.py:810-827) replaces QMessageBox with a non-blocking lambda, so it cannot catch the ordering.

Two side effects make it worse:
- shown=True is written before the first box. If the window is closed or the laptop restarts while that box is up, the watch never runs.
- watch=False is written before the second box. If the window is closed while it is up, the rollback is lost for good.

Severity: medium, not higher. It needs a faulty update that passes the finisher's check, plus nobody at the laptop during or right after the 3 minutes. If both happen, recording stays down at an unattended site until someone clicks OK. That is the exact safety net the docs promise to be automatic.

Fix:
- In show_update_result, call watch_after_change before showing the message, or show the message without blocking (QMessageBox with .open()/.show(), or the status bar).
- In _update_watch_failed, call tab.go_back(...) first. It closes the window and hands over to the console anyway, so the message is better shown by the console or recorded in the rollback reason/result.
- Write watch=False only after go_back has actually handed over.

One common case nearly fills the budget: the final segment's content hash is queued by on_sealed and runs an uninterruptible FFmpeg decode, so integrity.stop() waits the full 60 s. confirmed.title: A Return to service interrupted after record_transfer leaves the drive in limbo: refused for ever, never written

confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the return resumable. If the latest event for the drive is archive_drive_returned and the drive is still awaiting, finish the job: delete the paths of the TRANSFERRED copies, then clear awaiting. Alternatively, clear awaiting in the same step that records the transfer, and delete leftovers on the next attach.

I could not refute the core ordering problem. In _return_drive (worker.py 849-852), record_transfer commits the TRANSFERRED rows and the archive_drive_returned event in one transaction. If the process dies inside that window (service killed, Stop-Process by the update finisher, crash, power loss), the drive is still in _awaiting and is excluded from copying (line 354). A retry is then refused: last_swap_since_return (ledger.py 308-312) picks the newest swap_ready/drive_returned event, which is the return, so it returns None. The agent then sees the misleading message at 818-820: the drive "was not taken out with Swap ... Select the drive that came back from the office". The worker publishes awaiting_return for every awaiting drive that is plugged in (worker.py 1513-1514). _awaiting_text (line 981) also adds "To keep using it without an office copy, press Cancel swap." to the status message. Later returns delete only VERIFIED copies plus index and playlists, so that space is lost permanently and the drive fills early. The refusal message also points the agent to the wrong action. No recordings are lost (the office copy exists and the ledger is consistent), the chain is not broken, and copying is not wedged. confirmed.title: Any drive once picked as an export target becomes 'holds Sentinel recordings' forever, even when nothing was written, so it can never be set up
confirmed.description: load_known() reads the export branch's drives table: serial without model/size, unique_id, volume_guid, fs_uuid and the identity's volume_serial. Every serial lands in KnownDrives.serials, which matches any disk with that serial. ExportEngine._run() calls xl.upsert_drive(self.target) right after _check_target(), which accepts any writable separate volume (no marker needed), and before planning. A run that ends in NOTHING_TO_EXPORT ('Nothing was written to the drive') or fails during planning still records the drive. From then on classify() returns SENTINEL_EVIDENCE with the reason 'Sentinel's records show it set up a drive with this serial number before'. That is false, and erasing is never possible.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The agent plugs in a new Samsung T7 meant to become SSD_3, opens the Export page by mistake and presses Export. The result is 'There are no new recordings to export. Nothing was written to the drive.' On the Drives page the T7 now says 'This drive holds Sentinel recordings and will not be erased... Contact technical support.' The spare drive is unusable at the remote site.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In load_known, only use drives-table rows that have at least one export_batch with items written (JOIN export_batches/export_items, or a state past PLANNING). Or have the export engine upsert the drive only when the first file is written. Also match the drives-table serial together with model and size, as the drive_prepared records are matched.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the outcome, but the finding gets the mechanism wrong on Windows, and the trigger is much narrower than it says.

What holds: ReviewExporter._run (src/sentinel/export/engine.py:158-159) calls xl.upsert_drive(self.target) as soon as _check_target passes. That check needs no marker, only a writable separate volume that is not an archive drive. Planning comes after it (line 182), so a run that ends in NOTHING_TO_EXPORT (line 188-191) or a PlanError/OSError during planning (lines 184-187) still leaves a row in the drives table. load_known (src/sentinel/drives/known.py:116-133) reads that row with no check that anything was ever written. From then on classify() returns SENTINEL_EVIDENCE for the drive, and prepare.py refuses to set it up.

What is wrong in the finding: on Windows, identify_target (export/target.py:203-219, _windows_volume_identity) never fills serial, model or unique_id. So the drives row has serial=NULL, KnownDrives.serials stays empty, and the "known_hardware" reason ("...this serial number before") is never the one shown. The match comes instead through volume_guid (known_volume) and the identity's volume_serial (known_filesystem). The agent sees "Sentinel's records show it set up or wrote to this drive before." The result is the same.

It also cannot be undone. The tool refuses to set the drive up, and a quick format in Explorer keeps the partition, so the volume GUID still matches even though the filesystem serial changes.

Why the severity is low, not medium:
- The usual accidental case, pressing Export on a new T7 while recordings exist, actually writes recordings to the drive. The drive then really is evidence and the classification is correct.
- The false positive needs one of these: no new sealed recording since the last complete review export (that is, the agent exported moments earlier), the drive too small for the first recording (E-001), a sealed segment missing locally (E-006), or an OSError while planning. All are rare on a recorder that is running.
- Export is an admin-only button.
- The design leans fail-closed on purpose; the known.py docstring counts drives "exported to by" Sentinel.
- Nothing is lost or erased. The cost is one spare drive that cannot be set up at the site, and the workaround is another spare or technical support.

Fix: register the drive only once the first item is copied (move upsert_drive after create_batch, or into the first copy), or have load_known ignore drives rows that have no export_batches row past PLANNED with at least one item COPIED or VERIFIED.
verdict.evidence:
Code read: export/engine.py:155-206 (upsert_drive at line 159 runs before the Planner; NOTHING_TO_EXPORT returns at lines 188-191 and PlanError returns at line 185, both after the drive row exists); export/ledger.py:137-156 (upsert_drive writes serial, unique_id, volume_guid and the identity JSON); export/target.py:139-219 (the Windows identity has only mount_point, volume_guid, volume_serial, filesystem, label and drive_type, so no serial); drives/known.py:116-133; drives/classify.py:88-91 (reason wording); gui/app/drive_pages.py:589-600 (the Export page lists USB drives that are READY, so a new T7 can be picked).

Reproduced with a throwaway script in the scratchpad: built a fresh Ledger, called ExportLedger.upsert_drive with a Windows-style identity (volume_guid, volume_serial 1A2B3C4D, no serial), then ran load_known and KnownDrives.matches on a matching DiskInfo. Output:
KnownDrives(volume_ids={'{11111111-...}'}, fs_serials={'439041101'}, serials=frozenset(), ...)
['known_filesystem'] Sentinel's records show it set up or wrote to this drive before.
This confirms that registering the drive alone, with no export batch or files, marks it as holding recordings. It also shows the serial set is empty on Windows, so the finding's "serial number" wording and its suggested serial+model fix do not apply on Windows.

confirmed.title: With a dock that hides serials, two different non-empty disks of the same model and size are not refused, and typing ERASE proves nothing about which one is erased
confirmed.description: _refuse_lookalike refuses only when another connected disk has the same full fingerprint, which includes partition and volume IDs. Two FOREIGN_DATA (or WRONG_FORMAT) disks behind one placeholder-serial dock with the same model and size therefore pass. Both rows read identically: describe() gives 'Model, size, serial hidden by the drive dock'. The only confirmation is the fixed word ERASE, and the dialog only advises 'Make sure this is the only drive in the dock'. Picking the wrong row erases the other disk's data. The identity check does not help because it confirms the row picked, not the disk in the agent's hand.
confirmed.failure_scenario: The Sabrent dock holds two disks of the same model: one with someone's files that must be kept, one meant to be erased. Both list as 'has other files', serial 'hidden by the dock'. The agent selects disk 3 instead of disk 4, types ERASE, and the wrong disk is wiped.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When the serial is a placeholder, refuse erasing (refusal 'lookalike') while any other connected disk shares the hardware_key (serial, unique_id, model, size, bus) and is not READY/SENTINEL_EVIDENCE. Or make the agent confirm a content detail they can check, such as the volume label and used size shown. A new disk next to the current archive drive (READY) stays allowed.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanism. It is real, but I rate it lower than the reviewer did because several things soften it.

What is true: `_refuse_lookalike` (classify.py:322-335) refuses only when another connected disk has the same full `identity.fingerprint()`. That fingerprint includes the disk GUID, partition GUIDs, volume IDs, layout and filesystem serials. Two non-empty disks have different volume and partition IDs, so they never match each other. When the dock hides the serial, `check_guards` (prepare.py:173-179) accepts the fixed word ERASE. The comment there says "The lookalike refusal covers the second bay", but that only holds for two empty disks that are identical. So nothing in the code ties the row picked to the disk in the agent's hand. I reproduced this with the repo's own test fakes: disks 3 and 4 are both FOREIGN_DATA with a placeholder serial, both get can_prepare=True and refusal=None, both have the same describe() text, and check_guards passes for disk 3 with "ERASE" while disk 4 is connected. docs/09_BENCH_TEST.md:104 also says later builds "refuse to erase while two connected drives look the same". An agent could read that as covering this case.

Why it is not more severe:
1. Only non-Sentinel data is at risk. SENTINEL_EVIDENCE and READY drives are refused before the ERASE check, so recordings and the archive drive cannot be erased this way.
2. The scenario needs two FOREIGN_DATA or WRONG_FORMAT disks of the same model and size in the placeholder-serial dock at once.
3. Erasing is off by default (erase_enabled=false), and erasing foreign data needs administrator approval.
4. The agent has to ignore the dialog's explicit warning "Make sure this is the only drive in the dock". The docs also say to use the Sabrent dock with one archive drive at a time, and recommend separate USB drives, which report real serials so the serial-tail check works.
5. The rows can still be told apart: the list shows different drive letters, and the messages and dialog show different used sizes ("other files (1 TB)" vs "(2 TB)").

So this is a weak guard plus a misleading code comment and doc sentence, not a likely way to lose recordings.

Fix: when the serial is a placeholder, refuse with 'lookalike' while any other connected disk has the same (serial, unique_id, model, size, bus) and is not READY or SENTINEL_EVIDENCE. Also correct the prepare.py comment and the docs/09 sentence.

confirmed.title: Credentials file keeps the writing account's Full Control after the service is installed, so the recorder refuses to record (C-001)
confirmed.description: The fix for M2 (2026-11-10) creates the temp file with winacl.write_private_file(tmp, b""). That function uses private_sddl(current_user_sid()), so the file gets (A;;FA;;;<writer's user SID>). The next step, secret_file_acl_argv (commands.py:218-222), runs 'icacls /inheritance:r /grant:r SY:F BA:F svc:R'. /grant:r replaces the grants only for the SIDs it names, so the writer's FA ACE stays. setup.write_secret (setup.py:339-341) leaves the same ACE, and install_plan's credentials step (commands.py:304-306) does not remove it either. When the recorder starts as NT SERVICE\SentinelRecorder, WindowsPlatform.secret_file_problems (platform/windows.py:203-207) allows only SYSTEM, Administrators and the service SID, so the user ACE is reported. service.py:199-204 then treats that as fatal ('camera credentials file is accessible by other accounts', C-001, EXIT_CONFIG). I reproduced this in a scratch folder: write_protected_credentials with the real secret_file_acl_argv (an installed service's SID standing in) gave D:PAI(A;;FR;;;S-1-5-80-...)(A;;FA;;;S-1-5-21-...-1001)(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;FA;;;BA), and disallowed_grants reported 'grants access mask 0x001f01ff to S-1-5-21-...-1001'.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Documented deployment: setup (window, 'Continue as administrator'), then Install service, or on site 'Sentinel.exe set-camera' / the window Camera page 'Save and restart recorder' / 'SentinelService.exe set-camera-credentials' with the service installed. Every one of these writes camera.secret with the technician's FA ACE. The service then starts, logs 'credentials file: ... grants access mask 0x001f01ff to S-1-5-21-...', writes a terminal C-001 and exits 2. The SCM restarts it every 60 s and it fails the same way every time. The laptop records nothing; the agent sees 'Recording stopped. Error C-001'.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Create the secret with its final DACL and nothing else. Have write_private_file take an explicit SDDL such as O:BAD:P(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;FR;;;<svc>); the creator still gets the requested handle access on CREATE_NEW. Or append '/remove:g *<current user SID>' plus '/setowner *S-1-5-32-544' to secret_file_acl_argv, and use the same for setup.write_secret(readers=...) and install_plan's credentials step. Add a test that writes the secret the way set-camera does and checks it against the service's allowed set (SY, BA, service SID).

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. I reproduced it on this machine.

1. `credstore.py:56` creates the temp file with `winacl.write_private_file(tmp, b"")`. That function (`winacl.py:537`) builds its DACL from `private_sddl(current_user_sid())`. So the writer's own user SID gets an explicit Full Control ACE: `(A;;FA;;;S-1-5-21-...)`.
2. `secret_file_acl_argv` (`commands.py:218-222`) runs `icacls /inheritance:r /grant:r SY:F BA:F svc:R`. `/inheritance:r` only strips inherited ACEs. `/grant:r` only replaces ACEs for the SIDs it names. So the writer's explicit ACE stays. Nothing else removes it:
   - `setup.write_secret` (`setup.py:339-342`) uses `write_private_file` with or without readers, so it always adds the writer's ACE.
   - `install_plan`'s credentials step (`commands.py:304-306`) uses the same icacls argv.
   - No `/remove` or `/setowner` is run on the secret anywhere in `src`.
   - The config-folder icacls step cannot fix it either, because the secret's DACL is protected (PAI).
3. At start-up the recorder runs as `NT SERVICE\SentinelRecorder`. `WindowsPlatform.secret_file_problems` (`windows.py:203-207`) allows only SYSTEM, Administrators, `current_user_sid()` (which is the service SID itself) and the service SID. The technician's or agent's S-1-5-21 SID is reported.
4. `service.py:199-204` then adds "camera credentials file is accessible by other accounts" to the problems. Lines 213-222 make that C-001, terminal, `EXIT_CONFIG`. The SCM restarts the service and it fails the same way every time.

This hits every documented way of writing the secret once the service is involved: setup followed by install, `set-camera` or the Camera page with the service installed (`setcamera.py:117-126`), and `SentinelService.exe set-camera-credentials` (`__main__.py:353-356`). The result is a laptop that does not record. The fix goes wrong exactly when the non-technical agent re-enters camera credentials on site. The only way out is a manual icacls `/remove`, which the agent cannot be expected to do.

Severity: critical (the laptop cannot record). It would probably show up at bench setup, which softens it a little. But the agent's Camera-page path triggers it again after deployment.

Fix: create the temp file with its final DACL, for example `D:P(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;FR;;;<svc>)`. The creating handle still gets its requested access on CREATE_NEW. Alternatively, add `/remove:g *<writer SID>` and `/setowner *S-1-5-32-544` to the icacls step. Apply the same change to `setup.write_secret(readers=...)` and to `install_plan`. Then add a test that checks the resulting DACL against the service's allowed set.

confirmed.title: Return to service records copies made after the office copy as TRANSFERRED and deletes them from the drive
confirmed.description: _return_drive transfers and deletes every VERIFIED copy on the drive (self.al.copies_on(drive_id)). It does not check which of those copies the office actually copied. When the returned SSD is plugged back in and has any room, the worker attaches it straight away and copies the backlog onto it before the administrator presses Return. Those newer copies are then recorded as TRANSFERRED to the office destination (record_transfer, ledger.py:297), deleted from the SSD, and counted as archived (ARCHIVED_STATES includes TRANSFERRED). They are never copied to any archive drive again, and the backlog/A-004 reads 0. retention/manager.py:_copies counts TRANSFERRED copies as off the computer whatever the drive's presence, so with retention enabled the local originals become deletable and the recordings are lost completely. The same path deletes everything if an administrator selects the in-use drive by mistake: both rows read "archive drive SSD_x" and the size check passes.
confirmed.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a scratch test using real temp folders. SSD_1 holds 2 recordings and is swapped out to the office. SSD_2 is used, then swapped out as docs/10 says. Two new recordings are made with no drive in. SSD_1 is plugged back in and the worker copies the 2 new recordings onto it at once (drain -> copied, copied, idle). The return request result was: ok, "4 file(s) recorded as moved to Office and deleted". The ledger now has 4 TRANSFERRED rows on SSD_1 and backlog(None).segments == 0. The 2 new recordings were never at the office and now exist only on the laptop, while the ledger says they are archived.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Transfer only the copies the office could have copied. Record the swap/full index generation (or a cut-off verified_utc/copy_id) when a drive is prepared for removal or rolled over. In _return_drive, accept only VERIFIED copies verified at or before that cut-off. If the drive has copies verified after its last swap, or was never prepared for removal, refuse with "N recordings were copied to this drive after it was taken out; nothing was deleted". A simpler alternative: once a drive is swapped, do not write to it again until it is returned or Resume is pressed explicitly (persist this per drive, not only while it stays inserted).

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Nothing in the code limits Return to service to the copies the office actually received.

1. Copying starts as soon as the drive is plugged back in. `_swapped_drive` stops a drive being written only while it stays inserted. `_select` (worker.py:333-335) clears it after two scans without the drive, and `_full_drives` is also forgotten once the drive is out (worker.py:344-345). A returned SSD that still has room is therefore chosen and attached by `_step`/`_attach` as soon as it comes back. `_attach` also clears `after_swap` and `_last_swapped` (worker.py:545-547). The copier then copies the backlog onto it.
2. docs/10_OFFICE_TRANSFER.md (agent steps 1-3) tells the agent to plug the SSD in, Refresh, select it, fill in the dialog, and accept the UAC prompt. That takes minutes, and each segment copy takes seconds. With a single-bay dock, the drive in use is swapped out first (docs/10 step 1), so any recordings made in between become backlog for the returned SSD.
3. When Return runs, `_return_drive` (worker.py:789) takes `self.al.copies_on(drive_id)`. That query (ledger.py:127-134) returns every VERIFIED copy on the drive, with no limit by date or index generation. `record_transfer` (ledger.py:297-318) marks all of them TRANSFERRED. `_clear_drive` then deletes all of them, together with the INDEX and chain heads. Nothing records a cut-off at swap time to compare against.
4. TRANSFERRED counts as archived, so the backlog no longer includes those recordings and they are never copied again. They are no longer on any archive drive and were never at the office, yet the operator sees "All recordings are copied". With retention enabled, retention/manager.py:122 accepts TRANSFERRED copies whatever the drive's presence, so the local originals become deletable and the recordings are lost completely.
5. The wrong-drive case also holds. The GUI `_return` (drive_pages.py:466) checks only class READY and role archive. The CLI `_cmd_return` (__main__.py:192-268) checks only the marker, admin rights and that the copier is running. If the administrator selects the drive currently in use, its VERIFIED copies (possibly the only copies off the laptop) are marked TRANSFERRED to an office that never received them, then deleted.

Partial mitigations, which do not remove the bug:
- A drive that is truly full stays "full" after `_space_available` and receives no new copies. The bug needs a drive swapped out with room left. Swap allows that at any time, and Return to service accepts any drive.
- Retention is disabled by default (config.py:165). Without it, the local originals survive. However, the archive copies are deleted and the ledger falsely says the recordings are archived, with no alert.

Severity: high by default. The ledger is falsely updated, archive copies of evidence that never reached the office are deleted, the backlog alarm is hidden, and the agent gets no warning. It becomes critical with retention enabled, because the local originals can then be deleted.

Fix: when a drive is prepared for removal, persist the highest copy_id (or the index generation) on it. In `_return_drive`, transfer only VERIFIED copies at or below that cut-off. Refuse, and delete nothing, if the drive has newer copies or was never prepared for removal. Also refuse to return the attached drive. A simpler alternative is to never auto-attach a drive that was swapped until it has been returned or Resume has been pressed, persisted per drive.

- worker.py:341-345: `_full_drives` is forgotten once a drive is removed.
- worker.py:421-467: the reinserted drive is attached and the pending backlog is copied onto it.
- worker.py:545-547: attach clears `_last_swapped` and `after_swap`.
- worker.py:789: `copies = self.al.copies_on(drive_id)`.
- worker.py:807-808: `record_transfer(... all copy_ids)` then `_clear_drive(all paths)`.
- ledger.py:127-134: `copies_on` = every VERIFIED copy on the drive, no time or generation filter.
- ledger.py:297-318: `record_transfer` marks each one TRANSFERRED.
- retention/manager.py:119-122: TRANSFERRED copies count for deletion eligibility whatever the drive's presence.
- drive_pages.py:466: the GUI guard checks only class READY and role archive, not "not in use" or "swapped".
- __main__.py:225-245: the CLI checks only the marker, admin rights and that the copier is running.
- docs/10_OFFICE_TRANSFER.md lines 36-40: plug in, Refresh, select, fill dialog, UAC; the copier is running during all of this.
- config.py:165: retention is disabled by default.

confirmed.title: With two drives, 'archive swap' (admin window / CLI) never sees the swap complete: waits 10 min, then says 'not ready to be removed, contact support'
confirmed.description: _cmd_swap waits for state SAFE_TO_REMOVE, REMOVE_MANUALLY or ABSENT. When the swap prepares the idle full drive (_swap_idle, worker.py:950-970), the worker sets state back to COPYING (worker.py:967-968) and later UP_TO_DATE. Copying carries on with the other drive, so none of the awaited states ever appears. The unit test test_full_drive_rolls_over... even asserts state == UP_TO_DATE after this swap. The administrator window runs this command (drive_pages._swap -> _arc('swap','--timeout','600')) with the Swap button busy. After 600 s it prints "The archive drive is not ready to be removed yet. Do not remove it. If this keeps happening, contact technical support." and exits 2. That contradicts the status line, which says the full drive is ready to be taken out.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SSD_1 fills up and copying rolls over to SSD_2. The agent (an unlocked admin window) presses Swap archive drive. The worker prepares SSD_1 within 5 s (removal set, state COPYING). The command keeps polling, and the log shows "Do not remove it" after 10 minutes. The agent is stuck or retries Swap, which triggers the next finding. My scratch test confirmed status state == COPYING after the swap.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In _cmd_swap, also treat a fresh status as success when doc['removal'] names a drive and its drive_id differs from the one recorded before the request (or doc['removal'] appears where it was absent). Print doc['removal']['text']. Alternatively, have the worker write a swap result file with a request id, like return does, and wait for that.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. `_cmd_swap` (src/sentinel/archive/__main__.py:113-124) returns success only when a newer heartbeat shows state SAFE_TO_REMOVE, REMOVE_MANUALLY or ABSENT. In the two-drive case `_do_swap` sends the request to `_swap_idle` (worker.py:919-921: an idle full drive exists, a drive is attached, and the attached drive is not full). `_swap_idle` passes through SWAP_PENDING, which the command does not accept, and then sets COPYING whenever `self.att` is set (worker.py:967-968). It does this whether or not the eject worked. Copying carries on with the other drive, so the state stays COPYING or UP_TO_DATE. The only thing that shows the swap finished is the `removal` field written by `_publish` (worker.py:1421-1423), and `_cmd_swap` never reads it.

The command does not fail early either: the copier is still running, so the `copier_running` check stays true and the loop runs until `--timeout` ends.

The administrator window starts this command with `--timeout 600` and keeps the Swap button busy (drive_pages.py:312-315 and 349-351). After 10 minutes the log says "The archive drive is not ready to be removed yet. Do not remove it. If this keeps happening, contact technical support." The command exits with code 2. Meanwhile the status line on the page says "SSD_1 is ready to be taken out" (or "is safe to remove" if the eject worked).

The operator path (no admin rights) only drops a request file and does not wait, so only the administrator window and the command line are affected. That is the path the agent, who has the admin password, would use.

No recordings are lost and the drive really is ready to take out, so I rate it high rather than critical. The cost is a non-technical agent who gets two opposite messages, waits 10 minutes, is told "do not remove it, contact support", and may press Swap again.

Fix: before sending the request, remember `doc.get('removal')`, specifically its `drive_id`. In the loop, also return 0 when a newer heartbeat shows a `removal` entry whose `drive_id` differs from the one remembered, and print `removal['text']` (or the message). A sturdier option is a swap result file keyed by request id, as `return` already uses.

- worker.py:919-921 sends a swap with an idle full drive to `_swap_idle`.

confirmed.title: A second Swap press re-attaches and writes the drive already declared safe to remove, and prepares the in-use or new drive instead
confirmed.description: Problem (a): while the swapped drive is still inserted and nothing else is attached, _step takes the swapped_present branch and returns 'waiting_for_removal' without _clear_swap(). Only _no_drive clears the flag. A swap request taken in that state (_poll_control -> request_swap) stays armed. The next drive attached is immediately _do_swap'ed. _set_swapped (worker.py:853) then overwrites the record of the first swapped drive, so the first drive becomes usable again. If it is still inserted, _select attaches it and copies new recordings onto it while the agent believes it is safe to unplug. Problem (b): in two-drive mode, after _swap_idle has popped the full drive from _present and _full_drives, a second Swap finds no idle full drive and swaps the in-use drive (_do_swap). This also overwrites _swapped_drive, so the full drive becomes usable and is re-attached (status FULL).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Both cases reproduced in scratch tests. (a) One drive is swapped (REMOVE_MANUALLY), Swap is pressed again, and a new drive is inserted in a second USB port before the old one is pulled. The new drive is 'swapped' at once, the old drive is attached and receives the new recording ('copied', att == old drive). (b) Two drives: Swap prepares the full drive (state COPYING), and per the previous finding the agent presses Swap again. The in-use drive is prepared for removal and the full drive is re-attached; status is FULL with "Do not unplug the archive drive yet", and the agent is told to take out the wrong drive.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Call _clear_swap() in the waiting_for_removal branch, or ignore swap requests while _swapped_drive is set and nothing else is attached. Never let a new swap silently replace an existing _swapped_drive: keep a set of swapped drives, or refuse or ignore the second swap while one drive is waiting to be taken out, with a status message saying so.

- Neither the window (drive_pages.py:339-351) nor the CLI (__main__.py:97-124) blocks a second Swap while one drive is waiting to be taken out.

Case (a), one drive: the first Swap leaves state REMOVE_MANUALLY. A second Swap press stays armed. The agent then plugs the next drive into another USB port before pulling the old one. The docs recommend separate external USB drives, so a second port is likely.
- The new drive is attached and immediately "swapped".
- The old drive, which the agent was told is safe to unplug, is attached again and receives a new recording.
- Its swap-time index no longer lists that recording, and the agent may pull it in the middle of a write.

Case (b), two drives: `_swap_idle` leaves state COPYING/UP_TO_DATE. The admin `archive swap` command waits only for SAFE, REMOVE_MANUALLY or ABSENT (__main__.py:115), so it runs for its full 600 s and then prints "not ready to be removed yet". That makes a second press very likely.
- The second press finds no idle full drive, because `_present` and `_full_drives` no longer hold it (worker.py:960-961). It therefore swaps the drive in use.
- The full drive is attached again, and the agent is told to take out the drive that is not full.

Severity: no recording is lost. The internal SSD keeps each segment until a verified copy exists, and an unverified partial copy is not counted. But the copier writes to a drive that was declared ready for removal, and the agent is told to take out the wrong drive. The likely end state is the full drive left in place with a FULL alert, which leaves a non-technical agent stuck and confused. That is high under the given rubric, not critical.

Fix: in the waiting_for_removal branch (worker.py:417-419), call `_clear_swap()` and publish a message that the drive is already ready to be taken out. In general, ignore or refuse a swap request while `_swapped_drive` is set, unless an idle full drive or a non-swapped attached drive is the intended target. Never let `_set_swapped` silently replace a different, still-present swapped drive: keep a set of swapped drives. Separately, have `archive swap` treat a `removal` entry in the status as success (two-drive mode), so it does not time out and lead the agent to press Swap again.

confirmed.title: The window's Erase and set up is not tied to the drive the person saw: the command line confirms against its own new listing, so a different drive, or the same drive now holding files, gets erased
confirmed.description: The window's EraseDialog starts `drives prepare --disk <n> --who .. --admin --yes --serial-tail <tail>` (gui/app/drive_pages.py:416). It passes only the disk number and the typed text. It does not pass the fingerprint or the class from the row the person saw, even though to_dict() includes both. cmd_prepare then lists and classifies the drives again and builds `Confirmation.for_classification(c, typed)` from that new listing (cli.py:229-251). prepare_drive's checks for identity_changed and class_changed then compare the drive against a confirmation made a few milliseconds earlier from the same listing, so they can never fire on this path. That binding is the main protection against a change between confirming and erasing (prepare.py docstring: 'bound to ... what was shown to the person'). With a dock that hides serials, the confirmation word is always ERASE, so it matches any drive in that dock. With real serials, the dialog says to type the tail 'from the drive itself', so the tail matches whatever drive is in the person's hand now, not the row that was shown. The window also always passes --admin, so FOREIGN_DATA's administrator requirement is met without the person ever seeing the FOREIGN_DATA warning ('This drive contains other files (X GB)').
confirmed.failure_scenario: The agent opens the Drives page; disk 3 is a new SSD listed as 'blank' (the list is read only when the page is shown or after a command). The agent unplugs it and plugs in another drive, for example a personal backup drive with 800 GB of files in the same Sabrent dock, without pressing Refresh. Windows gives the new disk the free number 3. The agent selects the stale 'Disk 3, blank' row, presses Erase and set up, and types ERASE (serial hidden) or the last 4 characters from the label of the drive in hand. The command line classifies disk 3 as FOREIGN_DATA, which is allowed because --admin is passed and the window runs elevated. The typed text equals the confirmation text for that disk, so the backup drive is erased. The person was told it was blank and never saw that it holds files. Drives holding Sentinel recordings are still refused, because that check uses the new classification.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `--fingerprint` and `--expect-class` options to `drives prepare`, and make them required whenever input is not interactive or --yes is given. The window passes d['fingerprint'] and d['class'] from the row the person confirmed. cmd_prepare builds the Confirmation from those values, not from its own classification, so prepare_drive refuses with M-006 'The drive changed after it was confirmed' when the fingerprint or the class differs. Optionally pass the disk number and fingerprint to `drives eject` the same way.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding, and I reproduced it.

**How the window builds the command.** In drive_pages.py:416-417, `_erase_disk` launches `drives prepare --disk <n> --who .. --admin --yes --serial-tail <tail>`. It passes nothing else from the row the person saw: no fingerprint and no class.

**How the command line confirms.** cmd_prepare (cli.py:183-184) classifies the drives again. With --yes, its only check (cli.py:229-238) compares the typed text with `confirm_text()` of the drive that is at that disk number now. It then builds the Confirmation from that same new listing (cli.py:251: `Confirmation.for_classification(c, typed)`).

**Why the guard cannot fire.** check_guards (prepare.py:159-164) compares the fingerprint and class against that Confirmation. Both came from the same listing a moment earlier, so the "drive changed after it was confirmed" refusal can never happen on this path. That contradicts the prepare.py docstring, which says the Confirmation is "produced from what was shown to the person".

**Why the typed text does not catch it.**
- With a dock that hides serials, confirm_text returns "ERASE" for every drive in it (model.py:132-137).
- With real serials, the dialog tells the person to type the characters from the drive in their hand. That matches the new drive, not the row shown.
- The window always passes --admin, and an administrator window starts an elevated child, so the FOREIGN_DATA administrator requirement is met automatically.

**Why the list goes stale.** The list is refreshed only when the page is shown, when Refresh is pressed, or after a command finishes (drive_pages.py:261, 290, 419). It does not refresh when a drive is plugged in or removed, so the row can be out of date.

**What partly narrows it.** The window's length check uses the stale row's serial_hidden. So the bypass needs both drives to be the same kind: both behind a serial-hiding dock (the "same dock" case in the finding), or both with real serials and the person typing from the new drive's label. Drives holding Sentinel recordings are still refused, because that check uses the new classification. The warning "It currently holds about 1 TB of other files" is printed only to the output log while the erase runs, after the person has confirmed, so it never reaches them before the erase.

**Severity.** I rate it high rather than critical: it needs a stale list plus a drive swapped in under the same disk number, and Sentinel recordings themselves cannot be erased. But it does erase a drive full of other files that the person was told was blank.

**Fix.** Have the window pass the row's fingerprint and class (for example `--fingerprint` and `--expect-class`). cmd_prepare should build the Confirmation from those values and require them when --yes or non-interactive. Then check_guards refuses with identity_changed / class_changed when the drive changed.

confirmed.title: A recording that never gets sealed stops every later review export, which then reports 'no new recordings'
confirmed.description: Planner.interval() ends the export interval at the start of the earliest segment that is not yet terminal (ACTIVE or CLOSED), whatever its age. The finalizer gives up after MAX_FINALIZE_ATTEMPTS (5), and the service janitor then skips that segment for good (service.py:500), so it can stay CLOSED forever. From then on every export ends at that segment's start. The plan adds no warning, and the engine tells the operator 'There are no new recordings to export. Nothing was written to the drive.' (engine.py:188-191) even when days of sealed footage come after it.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced in a scratch script with 5 real TS segments, seg1 set to CLOSED with finalize_attempts=5. Export to drive A completes with only seg0 and its plan has no warnings. Export to drive B returns NOTHING_TO_EXPORT, although segs 2-4 are FINALIZED. On site, one segment whose probe or seal keeps failing silently stops all review exports from then on. The agent hands over drives that are missing everything after that point, or is told there is nothing to export.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not cap at segments that are overdue (finalize_attempts >= MAX_FINALIZE_ATTEMPTS, or not updated for well over 2x segment_seconds and not in the current run). Export past them, list them as a gap or warning ('recording could not be sealed; not on this drive'), and put them in a plan warning. At least, when the cap comes from such a segment, return a FAILED or attention result naming it instead of NOTHING_TO_EXPORT, and add an 'export_ends_early' warning to the manifest.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute it. Planner.interval() (src/sentinel/export/planner.py:202-217) ends the export interval at the start of the earliest segment in any non-terminal state. It does not look at that segment's age, finalize_attempts, or whether it belongs to the run that is recording now. plan() then returns None when start == end and no late segments exist, and engine.py:188-191 turns that into NOTHING_TO_EXPORT with "There are no new recordings to export."

Nothing else releases the cap while the service keeps running:
- The janitor (service.py:500) skips a segment for good once finalize_attempts >= MAX_FINALIZE_ATTEMPTS (5).
- Only startup Recovery (recovery.py:70-74) resubmits CLOSED segments, whatever their attempt count, so the cap lasts until the next service restart or reboot. On an unattended laptop that can be weeks.
- An ACTIVE segment in an ended run that Recovery flags as orphan_writer also stays non-terminal and caps exports the same way.

The trigger is realistic and anticipated. docs/05 row 25 lists "sealing fails transiently" with only 5 janitor retries about a minute apart. docs/REVIEW-2026-11-10 names "database is locked" while the archive process holds the write lock as a real transient. So a few minutes of lock contention during a long archive copy is enough to leave one segment CLOSED.

What softens it: the status shows V-001 "Recordings could not be verified" as CRITICAL, so the agent does see a problem. A restart lets Recovery seal the segment, which clears the cap. No footage is lost: it stays on the internal SSD, and later sealed segments still go to the archive drives.

The export side is still wrong and misleading:
- The first export after the stall finishes COMPLETE with no warning, although the drive ends at the stuck segment. Hours or days of footage are missing from what the agent hands over.
- Every later export says there is nothing new.
- Nothing ties V-001 to "your review drives are incomplete".

That leaves the agent stuck with a misleading message until someone thinks to restart, so I keep it at high, not critical.

Fix:
- Do not cap at a segment that is overdue (finalize_attempts >= MAX_FINALIZE_ATTEMPTS, or not updated for more than 2 x segment_seconds + 120 s and not in the current run).
- Name such a segment in an "unsealed_footage_not_exported" plan warning (manifest and status).
- If a cap still truncates the interval because of a stuck segment, return FAILED or an attention result that names it, not NOTHING_TO_EXPORT.
- Optionally, let the janitor retry overdue segments at a slow backoff instead of never.
verdict.evidence:

- planner.py:228-237: `if not main and not late: return None`.
- engine.py:188-191: the NOTHING_TO_EXPORT message.
- finalizer.py:37 and 138-145: MAX_FINALIZE_ATTEMPTS = 5; record_finalize_failure on any exception.
- service.py:499-501: the janitor skips segments with finalize_attempts >= 5.
- recovery.py:63-74: CLOSED segments are resubmitted only at startup.
- service.py:645-650 and status.py:99: overdue segments give a V-001 CRITICAL alert, "Recordings could not be verified" (SUPPORT).
- docs/05 row 25: transient seal failure, 5 retries.

confirmed.title: 'Return to service…' (deletes a drive's recordings) is not tied to the drive the person confirmed, and is offered for the drive currently being copied to
confirmed.description: _return() takes the label and letter from a list row that may be minutes old (letters[0]). ReturnDialog says 'This deletes the recordings from <label>', but the command passes only '--drive E:\'. archive return then reads whatever marker is at E:\ when it runs (archive/__main__.py:225), and the copier deletes every copy on that drive (worker._return_drive). Neither the GUI nor the CLI passes or compares the drive_uuid or label the person saw, although the list row carries 'drive_uuid' and 'label'. The page also does not check the drive's archive 'use' (in_use / full / take_out, available in status archive.drives), so the drive Sentinel is copying to right now can be 'returned' as well, which records its copies as moved to an office and deletes them.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Two archive SSDs are attached, and the list was loaded earlier. The agent selects the wrong row (SSD_2, in use), or the letters changed after a replug. They fill in the office form, tick the box and press 'Delete and return to service'. Every archive copy on SSD_2 is deleted and the ledger records the copies as transferred to an office that never received them. For segments that retention already removed locally, the footage then exists nowhere.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pass the expected drive_uuid (from the list row) to 'archive return' (e.g. --expect-uuid) and refuse when the marker at the letter differs. In the GUI, refuse or strongly warn unless the drive's archive use is 'take_out' or 'full' (it has been swapped out). Show the label read again at confirm time.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding, and the main harm is worse than described. Return to service is not tied to what the office actually copied. It deletes and marks as transferred every VERIFIED copy on the drive, whenever that copy was made.

Code path:
- The GUI `_return` (drive_pages.py:462-479) sends only `--drive letters[0]` from the selected list row.
- `archive return` (archive/__main__.py:225-237) reads whatever marker sits at that letter when it runs and puts that drive_uuid in the request. It never compares it with the label or uuid the person saw in ReturnDialog.
- `worker._return_drive` (worker.py:777-823) takes `self.al.copies_on(drive_id)`. That is every VERIFIED copy on the drive (ledger.py:127-134), with no time cut-off and no link to the index the office checked. It marks them all TRANSFERRED and deletes them.
- No check looks at the drive's archive use (in_use / full / take_out). The worker even handles the attached drive on purpose (worker.py:810-813).

Why the documented procedure triggers it: docs/10 step 1 says to plug the returned SSD in. With the one-bay dock, the agent must take the drive in use out first, so the returned SSD is the only drive. `_pick_drive` (worker.py:351-359) attaches any archive drive with room and starts copying the backlog to it at once. While the agent refreshes, fills in the form and answers the Windows administrator prompt, new segments are copied onto the drive. Return then deletes those too and records them as moved to an office that never received them. TRANSFERRED counts as archived, so they are not copied again. Retention treats TRANSFERRED as eligible whether or not the drive is present (retention/manager.py:117-122), so the local spool copy can also be deleted, and that footage then exists nowhere.

The finding's own scenarios are also real, but narrower:
- Wrong row (the in-use SSD_2): the dialog does name the label, so this needs an operator mistake, but nothing guards against it.
- Stale letter after a replug: possible but unlikely.

Mitigations that limit it:
- Separate USB drives with the other drive still in use and not full: the copier stays on that drive, so nothing new lands on the returned SSD.
- A returned drive that is truly full receives no new copies.
- Loss of the footage everywhere needs local retention to be enabled.

Severity: I rate it high, not medium. It is an irreversible deletion plus a false ledger record, and the documented one-bay procedure can trigger it. It becomes critical (recordings lost) whenever retention is enabled.

Suggested fix:
- Limit return to the copies the office had: copies verified before the drive's last swap or removal (the presence session's gone_utc, or the swap time), or exactly the files in the SHA256SUMS index written at swap.
- Do not copy to a drive that came back from the office until it is returned, or keep any newer copies.
- Have the GUI pass the expected drive_uuid (e.g. `--expect-uuid`) and have the CLI refuse when the marker differs.
- In the GUI, warn or refuse when the selected drive is the one currently in use and has been since before the office copy.

- src/sentinel/archive/__main__.py:225-237 (marker read at that letter at run time; its drive_uuid goes in the request).
- src/sentinel/archive/worker.py:777-823 (`_return_drive`: `copies_on(drive_id)`, then `record_transfer`, then `_clear_drive`; it also handles `self.att.drive_id == drive_id`).

- src/sentinel/archive/worker.py:351-359 (a drive with room is attached and copied to at once).
- src/sentinel/retention/manager.py:117-122 (TRANSFERRED is eligible for retention regardless of drive presence).
