I tried to refute this and could not. The finding is real.

1. **Restart only reaches the recorder.** In the deployed case (services installed), base.restart_recorder() (base.py:365-378) gets its control from select_control(). The first provider is _windows_service_provider, which returns a ServiceControl whenever SentinelRecorder is installed. ServiceControl (winsvc/control.py:54-123) has only is_running, start and stop, and its service name is SERVICE_NAME, the recorder. The guard at base.py:376, `hasattr(control, "start_archive")`, is therefore False. Only DetachedProcessControl (launcher/control.py:185) has start_archive. Nothing in the GUI starts or restarts SentinelArchive; a grep for ARCHIVE_SERVICE, start_service and sc.exe under gui/ finds nothing.

2. **The archive service never re-reads its settings.** run_archive_in_host (winsvc/__main__.py:548-575) loads the configuration once and builds ArchiveWorker(cfg). The worker uses self.acfg.backlog_alert_hours when it builds its A-004 condition (archive/worker.py:1377). No file under archive/ reloads the configuration or watches it.

3. **The stale A-004 reaches the operator.** The recorder's RecorderArchiveView.evaluate (archive/status.py:190-222) applies its own threshold, taken from the recorder's fresh configuration. It then also copies every alert from the worker's archive_status.json (status.py:214-216) and _merge keeps one alert per code. So the worker's A-004, still based on the old threshold, shows up in status.json even after the recorder's own check stops raising it.

4. **Archiving switched off at the last start stays off.** If [archive] enabled was false when the service last started, run_archive_in_host returns 0 (__main__.py:557-559). That is a clean stop, so the SCM does not restart the service. Turning archiving on in the window then restarts only the recorder. The recorder now builds RecorderArchiveView (service.py:755), finds no fresh heartbeat, and raises A-007, which turns CRITICAL after 30 minutes.

5. **Archiving off at install means no archive service.** The install plan adds the archive host only when cfg.archive.enabled is true (__main__.py:146).

**Workarounds and severity:** A reboot fixes the threshold case and the stopped-service case, because the service starts automatically and re-reads the configuration. A reinstall or repair of the service fixes the not-installed case. Nothing on screen tells the non-technical agent to do either; the button says "Save and restart recorder" and the result says "restarted with the saved settings". This is wrong behaviour with a workaround and a misleading message. No recordings are lost (the recorder keeps recording and segments stay on the internal SSD), so medium is the right severity.

I did not verify the claim in scenario (a) that the save is then rolled back; it relies on a separate finding. The earlier review (REVIEW-2026-11-10.md) does not cover this issue.

**Fix:** add restart_archive to ServiceControl, using the archive service name and the same SCM stop/start calls. Call it from restart_recorder when SentinelArchive is installed, or always when [archive] or display settings change. When [archive] enabled is true and SentinelArchive is not installed, say so and point to System › Service › Install / repair.

confirmed.title: Following docs/10 step 1 with two archive SSDs connected swaps the wrong drive and can stop all copying
confirmed.description: The office step says: if the SSD was simply unplugged, plug it back in, wait a minute, press Swap and take it out when the screen says so. This works only when that SSD becomes the attached drive. With two USB SSDs, the setup docs/09 recommends, the other SSD is in use, and _select() keeps it in use (sticky). The re-plugged SSD is only 'standby': it is not attached, so its index is not rewritten. It is also not in _full_drives (removed from it when it disappeared), so _do_swap() finds no idle full drive and prepares the drive in use instead (worker.py:918-948). The screen then says the OTHER SSD is ready to be taken out.
confirmed.failure_scenario: SSD_1 is yanked without Swap while SSD_2 is plugged in, and the agent follows doc 10 step 1. Swap prepares SSD_2, and the screen says 'SSD_2 is ready to be taken out'. If the agent takes SSD_1 (as the doc implies), SSD_1 still has a stale SHA256SUMS: copies made after its last hourly index are in verified_journal.csv only, so the office check prints NOT LISTED and says contact support. SSD_2 stays 'swapped' in the laptop and nothing is copied anywhere (REMOVE_MANUALLY) until someone presses Cancel swap. If the agent instead takes SSD_2, the wrong drive goes to the office.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Let Swap target a specific drive (the window passes the selected drive), or on re-insert of a drive that was removed unexpectedly, attach it briefly to reconcile and rewrite its index and mark it 'take out'. Update doc 10 step 1 for two-drive setups. Alternatively, have the office check also accept files listed in verified_journal.csv.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the main claim, and a reproduction confirms it. Two parts of the reported failure scenario are wrong, though.

**Mechanism (confirmed).**
- `_select()` (worker.py:316-363) keeps the attached drive in use while it is present (lines 351-352).
- A drive that disappears is removed from `_full_drives` (lines 344-345). So when the yanked SSD is plugged back in, it is only standby: it is not attached, not marked full, and its index is not rewritten.
- `_do_swap()` (918-921) prepares an idle drive only through `_idle_full()`, which needs that drive to be in `_full_drives`. Otherwise it prepares the attached drive (922-948).
- So Swap pressed under docs/10 step 1 prepares the other drive, and the screen tells the agent to take that one out.

**Reproduction.** Script: <reviewer scratch folder>\rep\test_rep.py
1. Two drives, the first one in use, then yanked. Copying moved to the second drive.
2. The yanked drive was plugged back in, then Swap was pressed.
3. Result: `removal.label` named the in-use drive, not the re-plugged one. The state was REMOVE_MANUALLY with the message "<other drive> is ready to be taken out".

**What the finding gets wrong.**
- "Nothing is copied anywhere until Cancel swap" is false. On the next step `_select()` attaches the re-plugged drive (it has room and is the only usable drive). `_attach()` reconciles it and writes its index (line 576). Copying then continues on it with status UP_TO_DATE, and the message still names the other drive to take out.
- The yanked drive's index is therefore not left stale. It is rewritten on attach. Only copies made after the re-attach and before an unprepared removal would be missing from SHA256SUMS.

**Real consequences.**
- If the agent obeys the screen, the wrong SSD goes to the office. That SSD was properly prepared, so the check passes and nothing is lost. But the SSD the agent meant to send stays on the laptop and is now in use.
- If the agent takes the SSD they meant to send (the doc says to take "it" out), they pull the drive that is in use without preparing it. That causes another unexpected removal. Any copies made since attach may print NOT LISTED, and the agent is told to contact support.
- No recordings are lost or corrupted, and nothing can be erased: return to service needs the office check plus admin authorisation.

**Severity: medium.** The doc misleads the agent, the wrong drive is prepared and the screen message contradicts the doc, but nothing is lost and there are workarounds (Cancel swap, or take the drive the screen names).

**Fixes.**
- Let Swap target the drive selected in the window.
- Or, when a drive that was removed unexpectedly comes back, treat it as the one to take out: write its index and offer it for removal.
- Reword docs/10 step 1 for two-drive setups.

confirmed.title: Files left behind by Return to service (failed delete, power cut mid-clear) can never be cleaned, and they block every later office check
confirmed.description: record_transfer() commits TRANSFERRED before _clear_drive() deletes anything. Several things can leave copies on the drive: a file that cannot be deleted (in use, antivirus, access denied: 'N file(s) could not be deleted; they stay on the drive'), a power cut or reboot during the delete loop, and carried_forward files from another ledger, which are never in copies_on. Their index and journal are deleted, so after the return these .ts/.framehash.txt files are listed in no SHA256SUMS. A later Return cannot remove them: copies_on() returns only VERIFIED rows, and _clear_drive deletes only those paths plus index, playlists and set-aside files. At the next office transfer the docs/10 PowerShell check prints 'NOT LISTED: ...', and the office is told not to return the SSD and to contact support. It can never pass again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Windows Defender holds one .ts open while the agent returns SSD_1. The log says '1 file(s) could not be deleted; they stay on the drive'. A week later SSD_1 is full again and goes to the office, where the check prints 'NOT LISTED: ...' and '1 problems'. Per doc 10 the SSD must not be returned. The SSD is effectively retired, and the agent is stuck waiting for support. The same happens after a 3 am Windows Update reboot during a long return.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make the clear resumable. Keep a pending-clear list (the TRANSFERRED rows of the last return whose files still exist) and retry deleting them on every attach and every Return. Include TRANSFERRED paths still present on the drive in the deletion list. Handle carried_forward entries explicitly (refuse the return, or transfer them too). Alternatively, list leftover files in the index so the office check does not flag them.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding, and a scratch test reproduced it.

In _return_drive (worker.py:807-808), record_transfer marks every VERIFIED copy as TRANSFERRED before _clear_drive runs. _clear_drive (825-850) deletes only these:
- the paths passed in, which come from copies_on() and are VERIFIED rows only
- the index files and chain heads
- playlists and set-aside files

When a delete fails, the path goes into `failed`. Nothing records it for a retry, and nothing tries again later:
- A second Return calls copies_on(), which now returns no rows. It deletes nothing and still reports "0 file(s) ... deleted from the drive".
- _write_index (1251-1329) builds `carried` only from previous index or journal entries whose path is NOT in known_paths(). known_paths() has no state filter (ledger.py:122-124), so it includes TRANSFERRED paths. A leftover file is therefore never listed again, even if the old index survived a power cut in the middle of the clear.
- Carried-forward files from another ledger are never in copies_on, so the clear does not delete them. The clear does delete the index and journal that listed them, so they fall out of the next index. This trigger is deterministic for any drive that had carried-forward entries.

The office check in docs/10 (line 24) flags every *.ts or *.framehash.txt file that no SHA256SUMS lists as "NOT LISTED". Lines 28-29 then tell the office not to return the SSD and to contact support. That drive can never pass the check again.

Severity is medium, not high. No recording is lost: the leftover file is an extra copy, and the office copy already exists. The triggers are uncommon: a delete that fails after chmod, a power cut during the few seconds of clearing, or a drive holding carried-forward files after a ledger reinstall. But when it happens, the drive is effectively retired and the agent is stuck waiting for support. The second Return's message is also misleading, because it says the drive was cleared while the file stays.

Suggested fix:
- In _clear_drive, also delete TRANSFERRED paths of this drive that still exist, so a later Return or attach can finish the job.
- Either refuse a Return while carried-forward entries exist, or keep listing leftover files in the index (for example as transferred_leftover with their hash) so the office check accepts them.

- ledger.py:126-134: copies_on returns VERIFIED rows only.
- ledger.py:122-124: known_paths includes every state.
- worker.py:1262-1273: carried entries skip every path in known_paths.

The elevated helper's Assert-Disk (commands.py:124-125) reads only Get-Disk's $d.SerialNumber. Nothing else in the helper reads Win32_DiskDrive, and no other code supplies the serial. The Python-side re-checks before launch (prepare.py:272-275) use the same parser, so they pass, and the helper then fails at the verify step with 'IDENTITY_MISMATCH serial'. Nothing is erased, because the check runs before Clear-Disk, so there is no data-loss or wrong-disk risk. The failure is safe; the drive is just permanently refused, with a misleading message.

Why I rate it lower than the reviewer's 'medium':
(1) Erase-and-set-up is off by default (policy.py:47, erase_enabled = False, owner decision 2026-11-10). The path is reachable only after an administrator turns it on.
(2) The trigger is speculative. The only real-hardware fixture (windows_dev_host.json: SATA, NVMe and virtual disks) shows Get-Disk and Win32_DiskDrive serials that agree, including the virtual disk where both are empty. The USB fixture is constructed, and there too both sources agree. On modern Windows both classes take the serial from the same storage device descriptor, so the case 'Get-Disk blank, Win32_DiskDrive filled' is plausible for some USB bridges but not shown.
The defect in the code is certain. Its practical impact is rare and fails safe, with a workaround: prepare the drive another way, or use a different enclosure.

Fix: have Assert-Disk apply the same rule. If (N $d.SerialNumber) is empty, read (Get-CimInstance Win32_DiskDrive | Where-Object Index -eq $d.Number).SerialNumber and normalise it the same way. Better: record in exp which source supplied the serial and compare against that source only. Also give exit-3 'serial' mismatches a distinct, accurate message instead of 'the drive changed'.
verdict.evidence:
Code read:
- windows_enum.py:56: ENUM_SCRIPT queries Win32_DiskDrive Index/PNPDeviceID/SerialNumber.
- windows_enum.py:181-184: dd = pnp.get(number); serial = norm_serial(d.SerialNumber) or norm_serial(dd.SerialNumber).
- commands.py:201: exp "serial" = ident.serial or "".
- commands.py:124-125: $serial = ((N $d.SerialNumber) -replace '\s','').TrimEnd('.'); if ($serial -ne $exp.serial) { throw 'IDENTITY_MISMATCH serial' }. $d comes from Get-Disk -Number (line 161), and the helper never reads Win32_DiskDrive.
- commands.py:189: IDENTITY_MISMATCH* gives exit 3.
- prepare.py:299-300: exit 3 before erasing raises IdentityChanged "The drive changed after it was confirmed. Nothing was erased."
- policy.py:47: erase_enabled defaults to False.

Reproduction: scratch script <reviewer scratch folder>/serial_fb.py. It loads tests/fixtures/drives/windows_dev_host.json, sets disk 1's Get-Disk SerialNumber to null (Win32_DiskDrive still has Z505GDE8), parses it and builds windows_expected. Output:
  listing serial: Z505GDE8 | exp.serial: Z505GDE8
  helper serial (Get-Disk only): '' match: False
The helper side is simulated by the same normalisation as line 124; the PowerShell was not run.

Fixture check: in both Windows fixtures, Get-Disk and Win32_DiskDrive serials agree for every disk, so the trigger is not shown on real hardware.

refuted.title: A RAW or empty-GPT disk is classified BLANK without any content evidence; behind a placeholder-serial dock a Sentinel drive whose partition table was lost or re-initialised becomes erasable by typing ERASE
refuted.why:
The code does what the finding says. A RAW disk whose serial is the dock's placeholder comes out BLANK, can be erased, and needs neither the admin path nor the serial, even when the ledger lists its (serial, model, size) as a prepared Sentinel drive. I ran it and got that result. But this is a deliberate trade-off that the project has written down, not an oversight:

(1) known.py lines 51-57 return early for a placeholder serial on purpose, after the 2026-11-11 field report: a brand-new disk in the Sabrent dock was taken for SENTINEL_1 and could not be set up. The comment states the consequence outright: "a Sentinel drive that was reformatted outside Sentinel is not recognised in such a dock (docs/04 §4)".
(2) docs/04 §4 (around lines 136-140) says the same thing in operator-facing docs, and the classification table there lists "no partition table" as BLANK on purpose. Rule 5 in the classify.py docstring does too. So the "uncertainty moves to the stricter path" rule is scoped to unreadable or unrecognised filesystems and partitions, not to a missing partition table. A disk re-initialised or wiped outside Sentinel is exactly the "reformatted outside Sentinel" case the docs already accept.
(3) The gap only exists behind a placeholder-serial dock. The recommended setup (docs/04, docs/09 "Recommended instead") is separate external USB SSDs with real serials. There the same RAW disk falls through to the serial/model/size check and comes out SENTINEL_EVIDENCE ('known_hardware'), never erasable. I checked this with the same script.
(4) The failure needs an office clerk to initialise the disk, which docs/10 forbids in its first paragraph ("Never delete, rename, reformat..."). In the scenario as written (the office copies, then the clerk clicks Initialize), a verified office copy exists, so nothing is lost. The office would also have had to see the disk as uninitialised, for example through a sector-size mismatch between bridges, and copy nothing. Only then could the agent erase the only copy, and only if local retention had already deleted the originals.

So this is an accepted, documented limitation, not a defect. Treating "placeholder serial + RAW + model and size match a known drive" as FOREIGN_DATA with a "may be a Sentinel drive" warning would be cheap hardening and would not bring back the 2026-11-11 problem, because that path still lets an administrator set the drive up. It is worth suggesting to the owner. Note that the admin step adds little here, because every erase already goes through UAC and the agent has the password.

refuted.title: If the ledger write fails after a successful erase or rename, the drive is changed but unrecorded, and a traceback is shown
refuted.why:
The code path the finding describes does exist, but the scenario it gives cannot realistically happen on the deployed laptop, so I am rating it not real (at most a low-priority hardening item).

What holds up:
- prepare.py:375 `_finish` calls `_audit` -> `Ledger.add_event` (db.py:703) -> `tx()` with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and `busy_timeout=5000` (db.py:450, 489). Nothing retries it.
- cmd_prepare (drives/cli.py:270-278) catches only PrepareRefused and PrepareFailed. `main` (cli.py:388) catches only DriveError. So a sqlite3.OperationalError would print a traceback after the erase, the marker write and the READY check.
- rename.py:131 is the same: cmd_rename (cli.py:329-333) catches RenameRefused and OSError, and sqlite3.Error is not a subclass of OSError.
- load_known (known.py:96) and next_label (prepare.py:209) read only drive_prepared and drive_renamed records.

Why the scenario fails:
1. The lock would have to be held for more than 5 s, and nothing on this system holds one that long. I benchmarked the real `ArchiveLedger.record_transfer` (the "Return to service" transaction, archive/ledger.py:321) on 4000 VERIFIED chained copies. The whole transaction took 0.41 s. A concurrent `Ledger.add_event` from a second connection waited 0.45 s and succeeded. The shipped configs use `segment_seconds = 3600` (config/sentinel.windows.example.toml:27), about 1-2 copies per recorded hour. Going past 5 s would take around 50,000 copies on one drive, which is years of recording. The other write transactions (recorder, retention, export, record_verified) are single-row or small. Each copier transaction also raises I/O priority first (`normal_priority()`), so background I/O priority does not stretch the lock either.
2. The window will not run the two at once. Return to service and Erase and set up both go through the drive page's OutputLog.run (gui/app/base.py:193). It refuses a second command while one is running unless that command has a stop_note, and the return command (drive_pages.py:481-484) has none. The agent cannot start a drive setup while a return is in progress, as the scenario assumes.
3. The other trigger ("a disk error") means the internal SSD holding the ledger is failing. The recorder's own ledger writes, which also have no retry, would fail first. An unrecorded prepare would be a minor side effect at that point.
4. Even in the theoretical case the impact is small. The drive was just erased and holds no recordings, so nothing is lost and no wrong disk can be erased. next_label also counts the labels of attached volumes, so a label can only collide after the drive has been unplugged.

So: an unhandled-exception path exists and is technically reachable by some unforeseen lock longer than 5 s. A cheap fix would be wrapping the final add_event in `retry_locked` and catching sqlite3.Error into PrepareFailed or a clear message. But the concrete failure the finding describes was not reproduced and is ruled out by the measured timings and the window's one-command-at-a-time rule.

refuted.title: A run that opens the output but never receives video leaves a 0-byte segment that is sealed CORRUPT and raises V-002 'damaged recording'
refuted.why:
I could not reproduce the scenario the finding describes. With the FFmpeg that ships with Sentinel, a camera that answers but sends no video never produces a seg_000000.ts.

The finding's chain is: the RTSP server answers, no RTP arrives, FFmpeg writes the segment header anyway, an empty seg_000000.ts appears, and it gets sealed CORRUPT with V-002. The step that fails is FFmpeg writing the header. To mimic it, I fed the recorder's exact output arguments (from build_record_argv) to the bundled binary, dist/Sentinel/ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe (n9.0.2). The input was an SDP file for H.264 over RTP on a loopback UDP port. Its sprop-parameter-sets were taken from a real encode, so the SPS and PPS were known, just as a camera's SDP provides them, but no RTP was ever sent. FFmpeg finished probing with "Could not find codec parameters ... unspecified size". The segment muxer then refused to start: "[segment] dimensions not set / Could not write header (incorrect codec parameters ?)". FFmpeg exited with an error and the run folder stayed empty, with no seg_*.ts and no segments.csv. Two other zero-packet inputs gave the same result: MPEG-TS with only PAT/PMT, and a raw H.264 stream holding only SPS/PPS. Neither created a segment file.

The SPS and PPS alone do not give FFmpeg the picture size. Without a decoded slice the muxer cannot open its output, so a camera outage of this kind ends as FFMPEG_ERROR with no segments. _end_run then sees segs empty and _remove_empty_run_dir removes the folder. Nothing is sealed CORRUPT and V-002 is not raised. The motion or schedule 'q' case fails in the same way. While FFmpeg is still connecting it has not opened the output, so stopping it leaves no file.

The code path the reviewer read is real. _register_new_files (supervisor.py:729) registers files of any size, and probe.py:86 turns a 0-byte file into a CORRUPT seal. So a 0-byte segment would be sealed CORRUPT if one ever existed. Only narrow cases could create one:
- The picture size becomes known from probed packets, but no keyframe is muxed within connect_timeout_s (20 s), because stream copy drops packets before the first keyframe. That means a camera sending only P-frames for 20 s or more, which is an exotic fault.
- A stop lands inside the first GOP (about 1-4 s), between the header write and the first keyframe.
In both cases the camera or stream really is misbehaving, so the alert is unwelcome but not dangerous. No footage is lost and the chain stays consistent.

Treating a 0-byte, never-listed segment from a run with media_s == 0 as "no footage" rather than CORRUPT would still be a reasonable hardening step. It is not the medium-severity, hundreds-a-day failure the finding claims.

refuted.title: A failed COMMIT leaves the ledger connection inside a transaction for good: all later writes fail, and the write lock is held across processes
refuted.why:
The finding is not real. The mechanism exists in principle: tx() at src/sentinel/db.py:497 runs COMMIT with no handler, so a COMMIT that fails but leaves the transaction open would stick. But none of the triggers can happen in the deployed configuration.

1. Deferred foreign keys: this was the reviewer's only demonstrated trigger, and the schema has none. A search of src/sentinel finds no DEFERRABLE, no PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys and no RETURNING. The demo relied on a feature Sentinel does not use.

2. SQLITE_FULL, SQLITE_IOERR and SQLITE_NOMEM at commit: in SQLite's sqlite3VdbeHalt, a failed commit (other than BUSY) calls sqlite3RollbackAll. SQLite therefore rolls the whole transaction back itself, in_transaction becomes False, the write lock is released, and the next BEGIN IMMEDIATE works. So a full internal SSD or a disk I/O error gives one failed write, not a stuck connection. The connection does not keep the cross-process write lock either.

3. SQLITE_BUSY at commit: the constructor makes sure the ledger is in WAL mode (db.py:429-441), and tx() takes the write lock up front with BEGIN IMMEDIATE. In WAL mode, a commit only appends frames to the WAL; it never needs a lock upgrade. SQLite's walRestartLog asserts that BUSY cannot happen there, and errors from the automatic checkpoint are not passed back to the caller. Committing with a write statement still running would also return BUSY, but nothing in the code leaves one running (no RETURNING, and plain INSERT/UPDATE finish in a single step). I confirmed the WAL behaviour: a COMMIT succeeds while another connection holds an open read transaction and the writer has an unfinished SELECT.

4. chain_head() reading uncommitted entries: tx() holds self._lock (an RLock) from BEGIN to COMMIT, and chain_head() takes the same lock. Another thread cannot see a half-done transaction, and since such transactions always end (committed or rolled back), the false anchor scenario does not follow.

5. The same COMMIT pattern in apply_timing_schema (ledger_timing.py:106) and ensure_genesis (ledgerchain.py:502) runs only inside _migrate during the constructor. A failure there makes the constructor raise, and the connection is not reused.

The suggested fix (roll back if in_transaction is still true after a failed COMMIT) is cheap, harmless hardening for the future. But no failure on the laptop leads to the wedged-ledger state described, so this is not a defect. At most it is low-severity hardening.

refuted.title: Return: a failure after record_transfer is reported as 'could not be returned', and a retry deletes nothing; non-OSError errors leave the CLI waiting 30 minutes
refuted.why:
The finding's main claim does not hold. It says an exception thrown partway through clearing leaves recordings on the SSD that no index lists, and a retry then does not delete them. I followed every step that runs after record_transfer.

(1) _clear_drive cannot throw partway through deleting. It builds the whole list of files to delete before it deletes anything (worker.py:829-833). cam.is_dir() and Path.is_file() return False on OSError instead of raising. In Python 3.14.3, the version in the venv, rglob catches OSError from os.scandir, including the list(scandir_it) inside it (glob._GlobberBase select_recursive_step / _StringGlobber.scandir), and entry.is_dir errors are caught too. Each chmod or unlink has its own try (836-843), and the second rglob, which removes empty folders, only runs after every delete. So "the drive briefly errors while the tree is walked" cannot interrupt the deletes.

(2) _write_index('returned') catches OSError on the read and on the write (1255-1261, 1311-1322). After record_transfer, copies_on returns only VERIFIED rows, so the media list is empty and the timestamp parsing that could raise ValueError is skipped. Playlist errors are caught.

(3) The only realistic post-transfer OSError is self.io.makedirs at line 812, which runs after all deletes. It fails essentially only if the drive vanished at that moment. The wrong part is the message: it says "could not be returned ... drive error" although the ledger already says TRANSFERRED and the deletes already ran. A file that could not be deleted because the drive vanished stays on the drive, but the success path leaves such files there in the same way (its message says so). That is the separate earlier finding about files that were not deleted, not something this path causes.

(4) What is left is minor. A non-OSError, such as a sqlite error from record_transfer after retry_locked gives up, escapes _poll_return. The run loop catches it (worker.py:266), so the copier does not wedge. If record_transfer itself fails, its transaction rolls back and nothing is deleted. No result file is written, so `archive return` polls until --timeout (default 1800 s). It then prints "has not answered yet ... contact technical support", and the waiting command can be stopped. This needs a non-lock SQLite failure, which is very unlikely, and no data is lost.

Fix for the leftovers: in _poll_return, catch Exception as well as OSError so a result is always written. Once record_transfer has committed, report ok=True with the delete counts even if a later step such as makedirs fails.

refuted.title: One missing or altered local original blocks every future review export with E-006, on every drive
refuted.why:
The mechanics are as described, but this is a deliberate, documented design choice rather than a defect, and the claim that support can only fix it by editing the database is wrong in the usual case.

1) Mechanics confirmed by reading the code (no script run). planner.py:424-428 _check_source raises PlanError E-006 for a playable segment whose file is missing. engine.py:465-473 _copy_file and engine.py:390-402 _check_source_sha raise E-006 when the bytes no longer match. A FAILED batch on the same drive is retried with its frozen plan (engine.py:164-178). removed_sources and _replan only react to local_deleted_utc, which only the retention rule sets. The interval start comes from the last COMPLETE batch. So, as the finding says, nothing moves the export past the bad segment by itself.

2) This is intended behaviour. docs/branches/req-review-drive-export.md:176 says: "A sealed original missing from local storage, or changed since sealing, blocks the export with E-006 until support fixes it. This is a design choice: never silently skip evidence. A missing CORRUPT file is only a warning." The different handling of CORRUPT and playable segments is therefore deliberate, not an oversight. The operator message is correct and clear: E-006 "A recording on this system could not be read for export", with the SUPPORT action (alerts.py:74). Recording, archive copying and retention are not affected.

3) The recovery claim is overstated. When a verified archive copy exists (the usual case, since the copier runs soon after sealing), support can restore that file into the spool path. It has the same sealed SHA-256, so _check_source, _check_source_sha and write_new all pass, and the export continues. No database edit is needed.

4) There is also a partial self-heal. Under disk pressure, retention (retention/manager.py:124-216) can mark that segment local_deleted_utc once enough verified archive copies on removed drives exist. The planner then names it as "footage_only_on_archive_drive" and goes on.

5) What is left: the file vanished or changed before the copier archived it, so no good copy exists anywhere. That is a narrow window, and the evidence is genuinely gone. Blocking until support looks at it is exactly what the design wants. There is no tool to "acknowledge a lost segment", so support would then need a manual step. That is a support-tooling gap, not a bug that loses or corrupts recordings or wedges the recorder or copier. Review exports are also a technician command ("export run"), so the remote agent is not left stuck with a dead loop.

What the finding proposes (skip the segment, add a manifest warning) is a reasonable product change, but it reverses a documented decision. It is not a fix for wrong behaviour.

refuted.title: A hung or permanently failing archive copier is never restarted: A-007 lasts until a reboot
refuted.why:
The facts in the finding are correct, but the failure it describes would not happen as stated, and the proposed fix would not help in the cases it names. So this is a hardening suggestion, not a defect.

What is true:
- The archive process has no watchdog. LoopWatchdog in src/sentinel/watchdog.py is used only by the recorder.
- ArchiveWorker.run (worker.py:259-274) never exits on its own. On any exception it calls _report_error and retries with backoff of up to 60 s.
- run_archive_in_host (winsvc/__main__.py:535-583) just calls w.run(). The SCM failure actions only fire when the process exits.
- Launcher start_archive() cannot recover either. It would start a second copier, which finds archive.lock taken and returns.

Why the finding's two cases do not hold up:

1) Kernel I/O hang that lasts until a reboot. The design note at archive/__main__.py:18-21 says a failing USB drive blocks a call "for minutes", not forever. On Windows, disk-class and USB-storage timeouts and resets eventually fail the pending request. Surprise removal fails all outstanding requests with "no such device". Once the call returns with an error, the step raises, `errors` goes up, and the loop retries and recovers. The finding's claim that unplugging the SSD may not unblock the call is speculation.
   In the rare case of a request that truly cannot be cancelled, the suggested watchdog exit would not help. A Windows process with a thread stuck in such a request cannot finish terminating. Its archive.lock handle stays open, so an SCM-restarted copier would hit the lock as well. Only a reboot clears that state, which is exactly what the finding calls the problem.

2) A step that raises on every pass. Restarting the process would only re-run _open() and reach the same deterministic error. The worker already reports it: ATTENTION status saying it "will retry automatically", A-007 after 3 consecutive errors, and an archive_error event in the ledger. The A-007 action ("contact technical support and provide diagnostic report") is the right one for a repeating software error, so the message does not mislead.

No user-mode hang path exists that a watchdog would fix:
- The loop's waits are bounded: _wake.wait has a timeout of at most 60 s, and SQLite has a busy timeout.
- The archive code starts no subprocess and takes no lock without a timeout. Grepping src/sentinel/archive shows no subprocess runs and no unbounded waits.

No data is lost while the copier is stalled:
- Recordings stay on the internal SSD.
- RecorderArchiveView computes A-004 (backlog) and A-006 (problems) from the ledger independently of the copier.
- Retention removes only originals that already have verified archive copies, so it never deletes unarchived recordings.

What remains is minor:
- A-007's action text does not suggest restarting the laptop.
- There is no "restart archive copying" button.
Both are improvements rather than bugs, and the second could not fix a stuck kernel request anyway. Severity: low at most.

low.title: An unplanned gap that runs into a schedule pause or motion standby is never relabelled, so the whole planned period is exported as a camera outage
low.description: _pause_for_schedule and _wait_for_motion only log events. _switch_gap is called only from planned reasons (switch_open_gap's default from_reasons), so an open failure gap (stall/connect_timeout/ffmpeg_error) continues through the planned period with its failure reason until footage resumes.
low.failure_scenario: The camera drops at 19:55 (stall), and the schedule pause starts at 20:00 and runs to 06:00. The ledger holds one 'stall' gap from 19:55 to the next footage at 06:00. Review exports and the gap table report an 11-hour unplanned camera outage, although recording was intentionally off from 20:00 and the camera may have been fine. The same happens with motion standby after a camera blip.
low.suggested_fix: When a pause or motion standby begins with an unplanned gap open, call switch_open_gap(at=pause start, new_reason='scheduled_pause'/'motion_idle', from_reasons=<any non-planned reason>), so the failure gap ends where the planned period starts (detail ended_by=schedule_pause). Update the ledgerchain rules if needed (closing an open gap with a note is already allowed).

low.title: The automatic diagnostic report on startup failure or supervisor crash is almost never written: it runs in a daemon thread and the process exits at once
low.description: _maybe_report starts build_report (PRAGMA integrity_check, CSV extracts, zip) in a daemon thread. On the C-001 path, `return EXIT_CONFIG` comes right after it. On the supervisor-crash path, ledger.close() and return come right after it. The winsvc host then returns from ServiceMain and the process ends, killing the thread. A partly written .zip.partial is never pruned (_prune only matches *.zip).
low.failure_scenario: The recorder service hits C-001 (e.g. the credentials file ACL is too wide) and the SCM restarts it every 60 s. Each start launches a report that is cut off, so data/diagnostics has no report although every alert says 'provide diagnostic report'. A .partial file may be left on each attempt.
low.suggested_fix: On the terminal paths (EXIT_CONFIG, EXIT_RUNTIME), run build_report synchronously with a time bound, or keep the thread non-daemon and join it (bounded) before returning. Also prune *.zip.partial.

low.title: A ledger that cannot be opened at startup gives a stale status (X-001) and exit 4, never D-001
low.description: Ledger(...) at line 180, _audit_start() and Recovery(...).run() at line 229 are outside any handler. An sqlite error (malformed database after a power loss, disk I/O error, an exclusive lock from a tool) escapes RecorderService.run before any status is written. ServiceHost maps it to exit 4 ('recording supervisor failed repeatedly'), and the SCM restarts every 60 s.
low.failure_scenario: After a power cut, sentinel.db is damaged. The window shows X-001 'The recorder is not responding' (stale heartbeat), and 'winsvc status' says the supervisor failed repeatedly. The D-001 'Recording database problem' alert, which names the actual cause, is never shown.
low.suggested_fix: Wrap ledger open, audit start and recovery. On failure, write fatal_status_document('D-001', terminal=True) and an event-log entry, log the error, and return EXIT_CONFIG (or a dedicated code).

low.title: FFmpeg that cannot be launched (quarantined or deleted after startup) is reported as a camera problem
low.description: Run end reason launch_failed (supervisor.py:433-436) goes into the generic outage branch. outage_code returns R-001 'Cannot connect to camera' or R-003 'Camera connection lost' for any reason except 'stall'. Startup check_tools catches a missing ffmpeg.exe only at service start.
low.failure_scenario: Antivirus quarantines the bundled ffmpeg.exe while the service runs. Every run ends LAUNCH_FAILED, and after 180 s the agent sees 'Recording stopped. Error R-003: Camera connection lost. Automatic recovery unsuccessful' and goes to check the camera. The real fault is the program files.
low.suggested_fix: Map last_end_reason 'launch_failed' to C-003 ('The recorder could not be started') or C-001 in outage_code/evaluate, or have the supervisor add C-001 to the service's fatal codes after repeated launch failures.

low.title: R-004 'Recording keeps restarting' counts planned run ends (motion idle, schedule pause)
low.description: unstable counts every run end with media > 0 in the last 10 min, including MOTION_IDLE, SCHEDULED_PAUSE and GRACEFUL_STOP ends. Also listed in REVIEW-2026-11-12.
low.failure_scenario: Motion mode with keep_recording_s lowered to 30 s and a busy scene: 5 motion runs within 10 minutes raise R-004 WARNING 'Recording keeps restarting. Contact technical support', although everything works as configured.
low.suggested_fix: Exclude planned end reasons (graceful_stop, scheduled_pause, motion_idle) from the unstable count.

low.title: Live view keeps decoding the 5 MP main stream and writing about 1.5-2.5 MB/s of JPEGs to the internal SSD for as long as the window is open, including when it is minimised
low.description: The preview runs whenever the request file is fresh. StatusPage (the first page, restored from last_section) starts LiveView in on_show, and the window calls on_hide only when the user changes page (window.py:317-323). Minimising or locking does not call it, and the Qt timer keeps refreshing the request. The service then decodes every frame of the full-resolution main stream (`fps=5` runs after decoding), encodes 1920-wide JPEGs at q:v 4 (about 300-500 KB each), and writes frame-N.jpg plus latest.json about 10 times a second into status_dir on the recording SSD. That is roughly 130-200 GB/day of extra writes, more than the recording itself, plus a continuous decode on the laptop CPU and an extra RTSP session on the main stream next to the recorder's (and the motion detector's, when stream_path is empty). The liveview docstring says 'about two frames a second', which suggests 5 fps was not intended.
low.failure_scenario: The agent logs in and leaves the Sentinel window open on Status for weeks (typical for an unattended laptop). The preview runs 24/7: extra SSD wear on the drive that holds the evidence, constant CPU load, and a camera with a session limit could refuse the recorder's reconnect after a network blip.
low.suggested_fix: Stop requesting the preview when the window is minimised, hidden or not active (changeEvent/WindowStateChange), and after a few minutes without user input. Lower the rate and size (for example 1-2 fps, 960 px wide), or keep frames out of the SSD (pipe them straight to the window or keep them in memory).

low.title: A date period edge in the repeated autumn hour: the period is applied twice, and the status says 'no time to resume is scheduled'
low.description: state_at compares date periods against naive local time (lines 301-303), so in the repeated hour a period whose start or end falls between 01:00 and 02:00 is entered or left a second time. _candidates adds only the fold=0 instant of each date edge (`_local_epoch`, line 358), unlike the weekly edges, which got both folds in the earlier review fix. The second crossing is therefore missing from the candidates. next_change returns None or a later wrong time, and pause_message tells the agent 'No time to resume recording is scheduled. Contact technical support'.
low.failure_scenario: America/New_York, [[schedule.dates]] pause 2026-10-31 20:00 to 2026-11-01 01:30, default record. Recording resumes at 01:30 EDT, pauses again at 01:00 EST (naive 01:00 < 01:30) for 30 minutes, and during that pause render_plan and P-001 say 'PAUSE from Sun 01 Nov 01:00 until (no change scheduled)'. Reproduced. A brute-force check of next_change over five DST zones found only this case.
low.suggested_fix: Evaluate date periods as absolute instants: convert d.start/d.end to epochs once (fold=0), and in state_at compare `epoch` with those, so a date period is one contiguous interval. Otherwise, at least add both folds of each date edge to _candidates (`self._local_epochs(edge)`).

low.title: P-001 says 'Recording resumes automatically' when the next change is to a motion-only period
low.description: _pause_for_schedule sets resume_epoch = next_change(), the first change of mode, which can be from pause to motion. pause_message always says 'Recording resumes automatically on <time>. No action is needed.', but in a motion period recording happens only on motion.
low.failure_scenario: Weekend pause followed by default 'motion' on Monday 00:00. The agent reads 'Recording resumes automatically on Mon 00:00' and expects continuous recording, which only starts at 07:00 with the working-hours period.
low.suggested_fix: Pass the next mode (schedule.mode_at(resume)) to pause_message, and say 'Recording on motion resumes on ...' when it is MOTION.

low.title: With the Windows default time source, a healthy clock can be reported as not synchronised (T-002) between syncs
low.description: When [service] max_sync_age_s is 0 (the default), the age limit is 2 x the 'Poll Interval' that w32tm reports. With the stock source time.windows.com,0x9 (0x1 = SpecialInterval, used when setup is run without a time server, winsvc/commands.py:438), Windows syncs every SpecialPollInterval (hours to days on a standalone PC) while still reporting a poll interval around 1024 s. 'Time since Last Good Sync Time' then regularly exceeds 2048 s, and sync_reason becomes last_sync_too_old, which shows T-002. Not verified on a live system: the module itself says the successful w32tm format is unverified.
low.failure_scenario: A deployment without a local time server, but with internet access. Windows syncs with time.windows.com every SpecialPollInterval, and between syncs T-002 'The system clock is not synchronised. Contact technical support' appears although the clock is fine. The agent calls support.
low.suggested_fix: If the configured NtpServer flags include 0x1, read SpecialPollInterval (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W32Time\TimeProviders\NtpClient) and use 2 x that as the limit. Or have setup always configure flag 0x8 without 0x1, or set max_sync_age_s explicitly at setup.

low.title: First open of a new ledger by two processes at once can fail with 'duplicate column name' or a UNIQUE error on schema_meta
low.description: _migrate checks `PRAGMA table_info(segments)` and then runs `ALTER TABLE segments ADD COLUMN local_deleted_utc`. It also checks schema_meta for 'schema_version' and then INSERTs it. Both pairs run in autocommit mode with no transaction around the check and the write. apply_timing_schema guards the same pattern with BEGIN IMMEDIATE, but these two steps are not guarded. The DDL block for segments has no local_deleted_utc, so every brand-new ledger goes through this ALTER. The constructor's own comment says the recorder and archive services open a fresh ledger at the same moment at first boot.
low.failure_scenario: First boot after install: SentinelRecorder and SentinelArchive both start and both create sentinel.db. Process A reads table_info (no column). Process B reads table_info before A's ALTER commits. A's ALTER succeeds, and B's ALTER raises sqlite3.OperationalError 'duplicate column name: local_deleted_utc' (or 'UNIQUE constraint failed: schema_meta.key'). Ledger() raises in that service: the recorder dies at start and relies on the SCM restart, and the archive worker reports an error. I could not hit the window in 15 barrier-synchronised trials, so the window is narrow. It is still unguarded.
low.suggested_fix: Put the local_deleted_utc ALTER and the schema_version check and insert in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT, as apply_timing_schema does: re-check the columns inside the transaction and use INSERT OR IGNORE for schema_version. Or add local_deleted_utc to the CREATE TABLE in DDL, so new ledgers never need the ALTER.

low.title: Two writers appending to chain_heads.log at the same moment can overwrite or garble anchor lines on Windows
low.description: append_anchor opens the log in 'a' mode, a separate handle per call. On Windows the MSVC CRT emulates O_APPEND by seeking to the end and then calling WriteFile, which is not atomic across handles. Two writers can append at the same moment: the service thread (_anchor_chain at service start, stop or periodic) and the diagnostics thread in the recorder process (build_report → append_anchor 'diagnostic_report'). The same goes for an administrator's diagnostic report from the window, a separate process. Both can seek to the same offset, so one line overwrites the other, or a fragment line is left behind.
low.failure_scenario: A critical alert triggers _maybe_report (background thread) at the same moment the periodic anchor is written. One anchor line is lost, or a fragment such as 'c_report' remains. verify then adds 'line N of the saved-fingerprint log could not be read' to every report from then on, and the lost head no longer protects against a later rewrite. Nothing is falsely flagged as altered, but tamper evidence gets weaker.
low.suggested_fix: Serialise appends: take a module-level threading.Lock in append_anchor, plus a short msvcrt.locking / LockFileEx lock on the file across processes. Alternatively open with os.open(..., O_APPEND) and write the whole line in a single os.write; on Windows use CreateFile with FILE_APPEND_DATA only, which is atomic.

low.title: Starting fresh by deleting sentinel.db but keeping chain_heads.log marks the new log ALTERED permanently (V-003, no acknowledgement); no deployment doc says how to start clean
low.description: ensure_genesis sets previous_chain_missing=True when chain_heads.log in the data folder holds any anchor. kind_rules then reports 'chain_restarted' as a FINDING on every verification, and status.json's old head adds anchor_mismatch / log_truncated findings. docs/07 line 211 says a fresh installation 'must archive the old chain_heads.log together with the old database'. The bench test (docs/09), which runs on the deployment laptop, and the deployment checklist never say how to start the deployed log clean: which files to move, and that status.json in status_dir also carries a head.
low.failure_scenario: After the bench test, a technician deletes C:\ProgramData\Sentinel\data\sentinel.db (and -wal/-shm) to ship the laptop without test footage, and leaves chain_heads.log and status\status.json. At the next start, genesis is written with previous_chain_missing. The hourly check reports ALTERED and V-003 'The recording log has been altered — contact support' stays on the agent's screen for the life of that ledger.
low.suggested_fix: Document a 'start clean before deployment' step: stop both services, then move sentinel.db*, chain_heads.log and status\status.json together to an archive folder. Or add a `setup --new-ledger` command that does this and records that it was done.

low.title: An ignored second Swap during a copy still shows 'Preparing the archive drive for removal. Do not unplug it yet.'
low.description: _poll_swap_in_flight calls request_swap(), which since 0.3.12 ignores the request while a drive waits to be taken out. It then sets ST_SWAP_PENDING with 'Preparing ... Do not unplug it yet' anyway. The operator window path (_operator_request) does not check 'removal' first and logs 'wait until this page says SAFE TO REMOVE'. Nothing is ever prepared; the state silently goes back to COPYING after the file.
low.failure_scenario: Two drives: SSD_1 waits to be taken out, copying goes on to SSD_2, and an operator presses Swap again. During the copy, the status says SWAP_PENDING 'Do not unplug it yet', then COPYING, and no swap happens. The operator waits for a SAFE TO REMOVE that never comes.
low.suggested_fix: Make request_swap() return whether it armed a swap, and set SWAP_PENDING only then. Otherwise publish the removal text ('take SSD_1 out first'). In the operator path, check arc['removal'] before writing the request, as the CLI now does.

low.title: An inserted awaiting-return drive raises A-001 'No archive drive is connected'
low.description: When only an awaiting drive is inserted, _step sets ST_ABSENT, and evaluate_alerts maps ABSENT to A-001 ('No archive drive is connected ... Insert the archive drive'). The drive is connected; it is held back on purpose. The headline contradicts the message and points the agent the wrong way.
low.failure_scenario: SSD_1 is back from the office and inserted, but not yet returned. The window headline shows A-001 'No archive drive is connected. Insert the archive drive.' even though SSD_1 is plugged in.
low.suggested_fix: Use a distinct state or condition (for example 'awaiting_return'), and an alert or notice whose text says the inserted drive waits for Return to service or Cancel swap.

low.title: A malformed line in the drive's verified_journal.csv (or a non-object index JSON) makes every attach of that drive fail
low.description: previous_entries() calls int(j['size_bytes']) on journal lines and doc.get(...) on the parsed index. parse_journal only checks the field count and the hash length. A non-numeric size raises ValueError, and a JSON array instead of an object raises AttributeError. _write_index catches only OSError around previous_entries, so the error escapes _attach on every step. The drive is never used, and A-007 appears after three errors. Typical causes are exFAT damage after an unclean unplug, or a hand-edited file.
low.failure_scenario: After a torn or garbled append, the journal contains a line such as '...,<64 hex>,12x4,Sentinel/...' (7 fields). Each attach then raises 'invalid literal for int()', and archiving to that drive stops with 'Archive copying had a problem and will retry automatically' forever.
low.suggested_fix: In previous_entries, skip any journal line whose size is not an int. Treat a non-dict index document as absent. Also catch ValueError and AttributeError in _write_index around previous_entries, and log a warning.

low.title: Swap retries forever when a stray .partial cannot be deleted or the index cannot be written
low.description: _do_swap calls remove_partial_file() with no error handling, unlike _reconcile, which logs and goes on. If _write_index fails while the drive is still present, it raises RuntimeError. Either way the swap stays armed, and every step re-enters _do_swap and fails again. The page keeps saying 'Preparing the archive drive for removal. Do not unplug it yet.', A-007 appears, and the CLI gives up after 600 s. Causes include a .partial locked by antivirus, a read-only attribute that cannot be cleared, or a drive left with less free space than the index needs (for example after reserve_free_mb was set low).
low.failure_scenario: An antivirus scan holds Sentinel/.sentinel_archive_probe.partial, or a leftover .partial, when Swap is pressed. Then PermissionError on every step, the drive is never released, and the agent is told not to unplug it.
low.suggested_fix: Catch OSError per file when discarding partials (log and skip, as _reconcile does). Bound the number of index-write retries for a swap, then finish the swap with a clear message: the journal still lists every copy.

low.title: Two-drive Swap of the full drive never rewrites or checks its index; a failed roll-over index leaves SHA256SUMS short and the office check reports NOT LISTED
low.description: _swap_idle relies on the index written in _roll_over. _roll_over ignores a False return from _write_index. The stale_index flag is set on the Attached object, which is then discarded, so the write is never retried. The full drive goes to the office without the copies made since the last hourly index in SHA256SUMS.txt. The docs/10 PowerShell check then prints NOT LISTED for those .ts files and tells the office to stop and contact support.
low.failure_scenario: SSD_1 fills, and a transient write error during the 'full' index write is logged and ignored. Copying moves on to SSD_2. The agent presses Swap and SSD_1 is prepared without a new index. At the office: 'NOT LISTED: ...ts', and the transfer is blocked.
low.suggested_fix: In _swap_idle, write the index of the idle drive again; it is still inserted and idle. Alternatively, remember per drive that its last index write failed and retry it before preparing it.

low.title: The Windows launcher maps every Start-Process failure to 1223, and a script that is too long raises an uncaught ValueError after the 'authorised' audit
low.description: launcher_argv's catch block exits 1223 for any exception from Start-Process (file not found, command line too long, policy), and prepare_drive then says 'Administrator approval was not given. Nothing was erased.' encode_command raises ValueError once the encoded helper exceeds 24,000 characters. A script run showed this happens at about 17 partitions (FOREIGN_DATA disks with many partitions). It is raised inside runner.run, after drive_prepare_authorized was recorded, is not a PrepareRefused, and ends as a traceback with no drive_prepare_failed record.
low.failure_scenario: A foreign disk with 20 partitions: Erase and set up crashes with 'encoded PowerShell script too long' and a traceback. Or Start-Process fails for a reason other than a declined prompt, and the agent is told approval was not given.
low.suggested_fix: Only map the cancelled-by-user error (Win32 1223 / the 'canceled by the user' InvalidOperationException) to 1223; exit with a distinct code otherwise. Build the plan, including encode_command, before the 'authorised' audit, and turn ValueError into PrepareRefused('too_complex', ...).

low.title: After clearing, the helper re-checks only hardware identity, which cannot tell placeholder lookalike disks apart if disk numbers change
low.description: Each step after Clear-Disk calls Get-Disk -Number again and Assert-Disk $d $false, which checks hardware only. The not_cleared check protects Initialize-Disk. Between Initialize-Disk and New-Partition, however, nothing ties the disk to the one just initialised. Behind a dock with placeholder serials and identical model and size (whose bays the field report says drop and re-enumerate), a renumbering would send New-Partition and Format-Volume to the other disk if it had unallocated space.
low.failure_scenario: The Sabrent dock re-enumerates during the erase and the disk numbers swap. New-Partition -UseMaximumSize runs on the other bay's disk, creating and formatting a partition in its free space. _finish then reports layout_mismatch for a disk that was never meant to be touched.
low.suggested_fix: After Initialize-Disk, capture (G $d.Guid) and require it on every later Get-Disk. Better, keep the CIM object or path from the first Get-Disk ($d.Path / ObjectId) and fetch the disk again by that instead of by number.

low.title: The elevated helper does not re-check for files on a BLANK or WRONG_FORMAT volume just before Clear-Disk
low.description: The final Python re-check (prepare.py:272) runs before runner.run. The helper's content check compares only partition, volume and filesystem IDs, which do not change when files are written. A drive confirmed as BLANK 'empty_volume' (empty NTFS partition) that receives files in that window (UAC wait, or a review export started meanwhile) is erased without the FOREIGN_DATA admin and serial path.
low.failure_scenario: The agent starts a review export to E: and in another window presses Erase and set up on the same drive, which still lists as blank. The export writes Recordings/, and the helper's ID check passes and clears the disk.
low.suggested_fix: For drives confirmed as BLANK or WRONG_FORMAT, pass expected_empty=true and have Assert-Disk refuse (PROTECTED files_present) if any volume root holds entries other than the ignorable system folders.

low.title: Setup gives a fresh volume only 3 s to appear, then says 'Do not use this drive. Contact technical support.'
low.description: _finish waits max(ctx.settle_s, 0) = 3 s (the CLI does not override it) for the new volume. Each ctx.enumerate() starts PowerShell and runs four CIM queries, which takes seconds, so in practice there are only one or two attempts. If Get-Volume or the access path lags, setup fails with not_found_after_prepare and a scary message on a drive that was set up correctly.
low.failure_scenario: On a slow rugged laptop, enumeration takes 4 s and the first pass still shows no volume access path. The agent sees 'The drive could not be found again after setup. Do not use this drive. Contact technical support.'
low.suggested_fix: Set settle_s to about 30 s for the real runner, poll until the deadline, and word the timeout as 'press Erase and set up again' (the half-set-up drive classifies as BLANK).

low.title: The two-drive refusal message tells the agent to pull the other drive out of the dock without making it safe
low.description: The shared_device refusal says 'Another drive is connected through the same device. Remove it from the dock first'. In a two-bay dock the other drive is usually the archive drive in use. Pulling it out without Swap or safe removal cuts off a copy mid-write and is reported as 'removed without preparing'.
low.failure_scenario: The agent follows the message and yanks the in-use archive drive out of the Sabrent dock while a segment is being copied.
low.suggested_fix: Say: 'Both drives in this dock would be disconnected. Use Swap archive drive for the archive drive, or shut down the computer before taking drives out.'

low.title: Rename: if the marker read-back fails, the volume label is put back but the marker keeps the new name, and the message says nothing else changed
low.description: _write_marker raises OSError on a read-back mismatch after os.replace has already installed the new marker (lines 77-79). rename_drive then restores the old volume label and re-raises, and cmd_rename prints 'The drive could not be renamed... Nothing else was changed.' The marker now says the new label while the volume label and records say the old one. os.replace can also fail transiently when the archive copier has the marker open for its scan (sharing violation), leaving a .partial file.
low.failure_scenario: Rename SSD_1 to SSD_4 hits an I/O hiccup on read-back. Windows shows SSD_1, the marker says SSD_4 and the archive status shows SSD_4, but there is no drive_renamed record, so SSD_4 can later be given to another drive.
low.suggested_fix: Keep the previous marker bytes and restore them when the read-back fails, and retry os.replace briefly on PermissionError. Report precisely which parts changed.

low.title: A CORRUPT segment whose file was missing is 'late' in every later plan: each export press makes an empty 'complete and verified' export instead of 'no new recordings'
low.description: The finalizer seals a segment whose file is missing as CORRUPT with sha256 NULL (finalizer.py:168-177). No export can ever contain it, so the late query (start_utc < prev_end, state in TERMINAL, local_deleted_utc NULL, not exported in any COMPLETE batch) returns it on every plan. That makes 'if not main and not late: return None' (line 256) unreachable. Lines 329-335 then skip it and add another 'corrupt_segment_file_missing' warning. The plan has zero recording items, and the batch completes with only README, summary, CSV, manifest and SHA256SUMS.
low.failure_scenario: Reproduced: insert a CORRUPT segment with warnings ['file_missing'] and no sha256, export to drive A, then export to drive B with nothing new recorded. Drive B gets COMPLETE, 'Export complete and verified...', 5 document items and the same 'A damaged recording file was missing' warning. The expected NOTHING_TO_EXPORT never comes. The agent hands a reviewer a drive with no video on it, and every later export repeats the warning.
low.suggested_fix: Exclude CORRUPT segments with sha256 NULL (or no file) from the late query once a COMPLETE batch has named them (as _named_as_archive_only does for archive-only footage). Also return None (or NOTHING_TO_EXPORT) when no recording items were chosen and every warning was already named.

low.title: A verification mismatch (E-003) on a file Sentinel wrote turns into a permanent E-004 'different files with the same names' on every retry
low.description: When the read-back of a file that this batch wrote does not match, _verify_item / _mp4_fail mark the item FAILED and leave the final (unsealed) file on the drive; _fail removes only .partial files. On retry, reset_failed_items makes it PLANNED, _copy_phase_item sees the file, _existing finds a different hash (or the MP4 fails its forced full check) and _conflict raises E-004. Same root cause as the item already listed in docs/REVIEW-2026-11-12.md (low, not fixed); reproduced here.
low.failure_scenario: Reproduced with a TargetIO that alters one byte of the first original after write_new renames it (a bad write). Run 1: FAILED E-003. Runs 2 and 3: FAILED E-004 'existing different file: Originals/...seg_000000.ts'. The agent is told someone else's files are in the way and the drive can never finish.
low.suggested_fix: Record in the item that this batch wrote the file. On retry, rename an unverified file Sentinel wrote to a '.bad' name (it was never verified or sealed) and copy again, or at least keep the E-003 wording and advise using another drive.

low.title: Resume treats a drive removed between files as 'a verified file is missing or changed' (E-003 plus an error event) instead of E-002
low.description: _recheck_verified uses self.io.exists(dest); TargetIO.exists is Path.exists, which returns False when the volume has gone. It then sets the item FAILED, logs 'export_verified_file_changed' ('A file verified earlier is missing or changed') and raises a non-interrupted E-003, without checking root_present. verify-content has the same pattern (line 789: 'video missing from the drive' -> content_check='mismatch'): the loop goes on and labels every remaining video 'mismatch' until writing the report finally fails with E-002.
low.failure_scenario: The agent unplugs the drive while a resumed export is re-hashing verified files (which takes a long time on a full drive), between two files. The window shows 'Error E-003: Files on the review drive could not be verified. Do not give it to a reviewer. Contact technical support' instead of E-002 'insert the same drive again'. The ledger records a false 'verified file missing or changed' error event. Re-inserting the drive does recover it (the retry re-verifies).
low.suggested_fix: When exists() is False, check self.io.root_present(self.root) and raise ExportFailure('E-002', ..., interrupted=True) if the drive is gone. Do the same in _verify_content before raising 'video missing'.

low.title: One future-stamped segment pins every later export's interval start in the future
low.description: interval() takes end = MAX(end_utc) over sealed segments, capped only by non-terminal segments. When nothing is recording (camera outage, schedule pause, recorder stopped), there is no cap, so a single segment whose times are in the future (wrong RTC at boot, or mtime-derived times from a wrong clock) becomes the batch's interval_end. latest_complete_end (ledger.py:208) is a MAX, so every later batch starts at that future time. All real footage after it is then handled only as 'late'. The coverage / 'unaccounted_time' check and the interval-based gap listing run over an empty [future, future] window, and the summary header reads 'Recordings from <future> to <future>'.
low.failure_scenario: The laptop boots with its clock a year ahead, records one segment, and is corrected. Later, during a camera outage, an export runs: interval_end becomes 2027-..., and from then on no export can report a period with neither video nor a gap (holes go unflagged), the header shows the future date, and every export carries a 'late_segments' warning.
low.suggested_fix: Cap the interval end at the current wall-clock time (plus a small tolerance). Treat segments ending after 'now' as clock anomalies: export them as late, flagged, but never let them set interval_end.

low.title: No FAT32 check: files over 4 GiB (1-hour segments) fail as 'review drive is full' on an almost empty drive, on every retry
low.description: _check_target and the planner never look at the target's filesystem (identity['filesystem'] is known). With the default 3600 s segments, an original or an hourly MP4 is over 4 GiB at about 9.5 Mbit/s or more. On FAT32, writing past 4 GiB fails with ERROR_DISK_FULL (112) and FFmpeg reports 'No space left', which is_disk_full / MediaError.disk_full map to E-001 ('The review drive is full ... Use a larger drive').
low.failure_scenario: An agent uses a FAT32-formatted USB drive with plenty of free space. The export fails E-001 on the first large file and again on every retry; a 'larger drive' that is also FAT32 fails the same way.
low.suggested_fix: In _check_target, or after planning, refuse with a clear E-005 reason when the filesystem is FAT/FAT32 and any planned file is at least 4 GiB ('this drive uses FAT32, which cannot hold files over 4 GB; use an NTFS or exFAT drive').

low.title: Uncommitted stuck-segment fix: a stuck segment with no start time is skipped from the caps but never named
low.description: In the uncommitted change, interval() now skips every _stuck() segment when computing caps, including ones with start_utc NULL (a CLOSED segment left by a crash). The footage_not_sealed warning query requires 'start_utc IS NOT NULL', and the coverage span is added only when end_utc is set, so such a segment's time shows only as the generic 'unaccounted_time' warning.
low.failure_scenario: After a crash, a CLOSED segment with no times fails finalization 5 times. The next export goes past it with no footage_not_sealed warning; the reviewer sees only 'Part of the export period has neither recordings nor a recorded gap'.
low.suggested_fix: For stuck segments with no start_utc, name them in footage_not_sealed with the estimated period used for the old cap (the previous segment's end, or the run anchor), and add that span to the coverage.

low.title: An unexpected status document shape crashes the 3-second refresh, freezing the screen on its last state
low.description: build_dashboard calls alert_view() on every entry of doc['alerts'] and on doc['alert'] without an isinstance check. It does 'overall in RECORDING_STATES' and 'not in HEADLINES' with unhashable values, and .get() on storage/open_gap/last_segment. _show_summary (window.py:444-447) and StatusPage (line 300 '.items()' on detail) do the same. I checked these: alerts=['x'], alert='x', overall=[...], storage='x' and detail=[...] each raise in refresh(), so every timer tick fails and the window keeps showing the previous (possibly green) state.
low.failure_scenario: Version skew after an update or rollback, or a hand-edited or partly written status from another tool, puts a string in alerts or a list in an alert's detail. The window stops updating with no visible error, and may keep showing 'Recording normally'.
low.suggested_fix: Validate types (isinstance dict/list/str) in build_dashboard/_show_summary/StatusPage, and wrap refresh() so an exception shows X-001 'status unreadable' instead of leaving stale content.

low.title: Any background task (e.g. saving a diagnostic report) is reported as 'starting the recorder' and blocks closing with a wrong message
low.description: busy_work() labels every running item in self._tasks as 'starting the recorder', but save_report() adds its Task to the same list (line 511). closeEvent then refuses with 'Wait until the recorder has been restarted… Closing now would leave it stopped'. UpdatesTab._ready refuses updates with 'starting the recorder'. Finished tasks are also never removed.
low.failure_scenario: The agent saves a diagnostic report (which takes a while: ledger integrity and chain check) and tries to close the window or apply an update. The window says the recorder is being restarted, which is false and alarming.
low.suggested_fix: Track the setup-start task separately (or give Tasks a label), and drop finished tasks from the list.

low.title: 'Stop it and go on' fails with 'did not stop' if the waiting command finished while the question was open
low.description: _offer_stop runs box.exec() (nested event loop). If the swap command finishes meanwhile, cur.kill() does nothing and QProcess.waitForFinished() returns False for a process that is already finished. The user is then told it 'did not stop. Try again in a moment.' and the command they asked for is not run.
low.failure_scenario: A Swap waits; the agent presses Return to service, and the swap completes while the question box is open. Clicking 'Stop it and go on' shows 'did not stop' and nothing happens.
low.suggested_fix: After the box, return True if not cur.running(). Only call waitForFinished when it is still running.

low.title: Drives page says 'Archive copying is not enabled' and refuses Swap whenever the recorder's status is missing
low.description: on_status derives everything from the recorder's status.json. With no document (recorder stopped, missing status, or a terminal C-001 doc without an archive section), arc is {}. The page then says 'Archive copying is not enabled in the settings.' and sets _arc_running=False, so _swap shows COPIER_NOT_RUNNING even for an administrator. The archive copier is a separate service and may well be running; the CLI checks archive_status.json itself.
low.failure_scenario: The recorder service is down (for example camera-related crash loop). The copier is fine and the agent needs to swap a full drive. The page tells them archive copying is not enabled and refuses the swap. As an administrator the swap would work.
low.suggested_fix: When read.doc is None or stale, say 'Archive state unknown (recorder status not available)'. For administrators, let the CLI decide (it checks the copier's own status).

low.title: Operator-visible 'Archive details' / 'Archive problems' read the service-only data folder and mislead
low.description: Both buttons are enabled for operators. 'archive status' reads data_path/archive_status.json, which operators cannot read. read_archive_status turns the PermissionError into None, and the command prints 'Archive copying has not run yet.' 'Archive problems' opens Ledger(data_path/sentinel.db) read-write and fails with a traceback (exit 1).
low.failure_scenario: An operator asks for Archive details while copying is working and is told archive copying has never run.
low.suggested_fix: Disable both for non-administrators (or show the archive section of status.json instead). In _cmd_status, distinguish 'no file' from 'cannot read'.

low.title: Saving archive settings does not restart the SentinelArchive service
low.description: restart_recorder() restarts only the recorder service. The winsvc ServiceControl has no start_archive or restart for the copier, so archive.enabled and other [archive] settings saved on the Storage page are not applied to a running copier until reboot, even though the page says 'Save and restart recorder' and the window reports success.
low.failure_scenario: An administrator turns 'Copy every recording to the archive drive' off. The copier service keeps copying to and verifying the drive with the old settings until the next reboot.
low.suggested_fix: For the service control, also restart (stop and start) the SentinelArchive service when [archive] or [drives] changed.

low.title: Read-only bar offers 'Unlock…' even when administrator use was refused because of the config location
low.description: When admin_config_problem refuses administrator rights, the window hides its own Unlock button. Every settings page's ReadOnlyBar still shows 'Changing … needs Windows administrator rights' with an Unlock button, which reopens the window elevated into the same refusal.
low.failure_scenario: The agent with the admin password presses Unlock, approves UAC, and gets the same read-only window again, without being told that the real reason is the config file's permissions.
low.suggested_fix: Pass admin_refused into Ctx. In ReadOnlyBar, show the refusal reason and hide Unlock when set.

low.title: 'update rollback' never pauses, so its refusal messages vanish when the window starts it (window closed, nothing reopened)
low.description: The window's Go back, including the automatic rollback after a failed 3-minute update watch, runs 'Sentinel update rollback --yes' in a new console (update_page.start_detached_console) and closes itself (close_for_update). cmd_rollback prints its refusals and returns at once: 'No previous version…', the _busy 'Another update or rollback started less than an hour ago…', and the new 'did not go back … Recording was started again / could not be started' message. Unlike cmd_apply it never calls _pause(), so the console closes as soon as it prints. The Sentinel window was closed by the hand-over and is not reopened on these paths.
low.failure_scenario: An update fails and leaves pending.json (a known issue). The agent, or the watch, presses Go back. The console prints the 'busy' refusal and disappears within a second, and the Sentinel window is gone. The agent sees the program vanish with no explanation.
low.suggested_fix: Call _pause() on every refusal path in cmd_rollback, as cmd_apply does. When the window handed over, reopen Sentinel.exe on refusal (Start-Process or Popen of the launcher).

low.title: An OSError while staging (disk full, file locked by antivirus) crashes 'update apply' with a traceback in a console that closes at once
low.description: stage() builds a full copy of the program folder (~355 MB) on the system drive and re-raises any OSError after removing the partial folder (apply.py stage, 'except BaseException: rmtree; raise'). cmd_apply catches only UpdateRefused. A disk-full error or a PermissionError opening an installed file therefore ends the process with a Python traceback and no _pause(), and the console (CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE, from the window) closes immediately. Recording is not affected (it is not stopped yet), but the window has already closed for the update and is not reopened. Nothing tells the agent why. There is also no free-space check before staging on the drive the recorder writes to.
low.failure_scenario: The internal SSD is close to full (recordings), so staging fails with 'No space left on device'. The console flashes a traceback and closes, and the Sentinel window is gone. The agent cannot tell whether the update happened.
low.suggested_fix: Catch OSError around stage() and report it as UpdateRefused ('Not enough space or a file could not be read: … Nothing was changed.'), which pauses. Check free space (planned bytes plus a margin, above [storage] warning_free_gb) before staging. Reopen the window on refusal when it handed over.

low.title: Configuration accepts NaN and infinity for timeouts, intervals and space limits (TOML 'nan'/'inf'), which disables watchdog, stall detection or retention
low.description: Every numeric check is a comparison: 'getattr(rec, name) <= 0', 'any(v <= 0 …)' for the [service] intervals, 'watchdog_timeout_s < 5.0', 'critical_free_gb < 0 or warning_free_gb < critical_free_gb', the [archive] '<= 0' and 'reserve_free_mb < 0' checks, and the retention checks. Comparisons with NaN are always False, and inf passes too. TOML allows nan, inf and +inf. Verified with load_config_dict: stall_timeout_s = nan, connect_timeout_s = inf, watchdog_timeout_s = nan, poll_interval_s = nan and critical_free_gb = nan are all accepted.
low.failure_scenario: A technician writes watchdog_timeout_s = nan or stall_timeout_s = nan: the watchdog or stall detection never fires, and a wedged recorder is never restarted. poll_interval_s = nan or inf makes time.sleep raise inside the service (crash loop with no C-001). [archive] reserve_free_mb = inf overflows int() in ArchiveWorker.__init__ (archive service crash loop). A NaN retention floor never frees space.
low.suggested_fix: In _build, reject non-finite floats: 'if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value): raise ConfigError(f"[{section}] {name} must be a finite number")'.
