low.title: 'winsvc status' always reports the spool, data and log folders as 'WIDER THAN EXPECTED' once the archive service is installed (deployed default)
low.description: _dir_report allows only SYSTEM, Administrators and the recorder SID. The install plan itself grants NT SERVICE\SentinelArchive RX on spool and M on data and logs (commands.archive_service_steps). disallowed_grants counts FILE_READ_DATA as significant, so a correct installation always prints 'WIDER THAN EXPECTED: grants access mask … to S-1-5-80-… (a service account)' for all three folders. Bench step 1.9 (docs/09) expects 'folders OK' from System › Service › Check service.
low.failure_scenario: After a correct install the technician runs Check service and sees three 'WIDER THAN EXPECTED' lines. The bench step fails, or someone 'fixes' it by removing the archive service's access, which then breaks archiving (A-007).
low.suggested_fix: Add service_sid(ARCHIVE_SERVICE_NAME) to the allowed set in _dir_report when the archive service is installed. Better: check the exact expected rights per folder (archive RX on spool, M on data and logs).

low.title: Uninstall gives up after 180 s while a normal recorder stop may take up to the service's 600 s stop deadline; the service is left registered and stopped
low.description: uninstall_plan waits 'up to 3 minutes' (wait_stopped, timeout_s=180) for each service, then runs 'sc delete'. The update code was just changed to wait 660 s because a normal stop (sealing an hour-long segment, content-hash worker) can take minutes, bounded only by ServiceHost.stop_deadline_s = 600. When the 180 s wait expires, execute() stops at 'service still STOP_PENDING' and 'Removal stopped at the failed step above.' The service finishes stopping later and stays stopped, still registered. This is also the path a technician must take for a reinstall, because install refuses on an installed service.
low.failure_scenario: The technician removes the service to reinstall it shortly after the top of the hour. The wait fails after 180 s, the removal stops half-way and recording is stopped. If they then run install, it refuses with 'already installed'.
low.suggested_fix: Use the same bound as the update (STOP_TIMEOUT_S, 660 s) with progress output. If it still times out, say that the service is still stopping and that removal should be run again in a few minutes.

low.title: Files left on a drive after Return to service make every later office check fail with NOT LISTED
low.description: When _clear_drive cannot delete a copy (failed, for example the file is held open by antivirus), the return still succeeds ('N file(s) could not be deleted; they stay on the drive'), and the ledger row is TRANSFERRED. From then on _write_index lists only VERIFIED copies plus 'carried' entries, and carried leaves out every path in known_paths, which includes TRANSFERRED rows (lines 1353-1364). So the leftover .ts or .framehash.txt is never in SHA256SUMS.txt again, and is never deleted later either. The office check in docs/10 step 5 reports every .ts or .framehash.txt that is not listed as 'NOT LISTED' and says not to return the SSD and to contact support. The same leftovers come from the interrupted return above.
low.failure_scenario: At the first return, 2 files cannot be deleted. On every later trip of that SSD the office check ends 'N files checked, 2 problems' with NOT LISTED lines. Per docs/10 the SSD must then not be returned to service, so the drive is out of rotation until support intervenes.
low.suggested_fix: Retry deleting the leftover TRANSFERRED paths on attach, or at the next return. Alternatively, list them in the index and SHA256SUMS under a 'transferred_leftover' section the office check accepts.

low.title: After the clock is set back, an old status heartbeat counts as fresh, which can hide a dead recorder or copier
low.description: read_status computes age = time.time() - heartbeat_epoch and only treats age > max_age_s as stale. A heartbeat written while the clock was hours ahead has a negative age after the clock is corrected, so it counts as fresh until the clock catches up. The same applies to archive/status.py copier_running (line 141), RecorderArchiveView.evaluate (lines 201-202) and launcher/control.archive_alive (lines 98-99). It is harmless while the writer keeps writing. It matters when the writer dies or never starts after the correction, typically scenario 8 combined with scenario 1.
low.failure_scenario: The laptop runs for a day with the clock 5 h fast. Power is lost, and at boot the clock is right (the RTC or time sync fixed it). The recorder service then fails before writing a new status, or sits in long start-up recovery. For up to 5 h the window shows the last status, 'Recording normally', instead of X-001, and the copier counts as 'running', so A-007 is suppressed.
low.suggested_fix: Treat a heartbeat more than a small tolerance in the future (for example age < -max_age_s) as stale or unknown, and say so. Better, also compare the writer's monotonic or boot ID, or the file mtime.

low.title: Return to service depends on the swap event, which is written best-effort after the drive is already locked out
low.description: _do_swap and _swap_idle persist swapped_drive.json and awaiting_return.json first, and only then write the 'archive_swap_ready' event through _event(). _event swallows every exception (lines 1559-1563). _return_drive now requires that event (last_swap_since_return). If the ledger write fails (locked beyond retry, disk error) or the process dies between _set_awaiting and _event, the drive is awaiting (never written) but no swap event exists, so every Return to service is refused with 'was not taken out with Swap archive drive'.
low.failure_scenario: The ledger is briefly locked or failing just as the agent's Swap completes. The SSD goes to the office and comes back, and Return to service is refused. The drive also stays excluded from copying, and Cancel swap, the only way out, is hidden in the window.
low.suggested_fix: Write the swap event first, in the ledger (with last_copy_id), and only then persist swapped/awaiting. Alternatively, store last_copy_id in awaiting_return.json and let _return_drive fall back to it.

low.title: Agent is told to wait for 'SAFE TO REMOVE', which never appears in the shipped build
low.description: Production builds the worker with ManualRemovalFallback (no ejector is ever passed in run_archive_in_host), whose eject() always returns ejected=False. ST_SAFE / 'SAFE TO REMOVE ARCHIVE DRIVE.' is therefore never shown. Yet MSG_FULL (lines 110-111), the A-002 action (alerts.py:105-107), the window's swap log ('wait until this page says SAFE TO REMOVE', drive_pages.py:335-337), the swap tooltip, and docs/09 step 5.5 ('SAFE TO REMOVE before removal') all tell the agent to wait for it. With two drives present, _removal_text (lines 1070-1073) also says 'Do not use Windows' Safely Remove Hardware ... in a two-bay dock that would also stop the other drive'. That is wrong for the separate USB SSDs docs/09 now recommends.
low.failure_scenario: With the archive drive full, the agent presses Swap and waits for 'SAFE TO REMOVE' as A-002 instructs. The page shows 'remove with Windows' plus the Safely Remove instruction, and an agent following the alert text keeps waiting, or pulls the drive. With two separate USB SSDs the agent is told not to use Safely Remove Hardware at all.
low.suggested_fix: Make the wording match the build: 'wait until this page says what to do, then use Safely Remove Hardware', as MSG for REMOVE_MANUALLY already does. Base the two-drive advice on whether both drives sit behind the same USB device, not on how many are present. Update docs/09 step 5.5.

low.title: docs/10 says Windows asks for the admin password at 'Delete and return to service', but the button is greyed out unless the window was unlocked first
low.description: The laptop steps say: press Return to service…, fill in, press Delete and return to service, 'Windows asks for the administrator password.' In drive_pages.py:281-282 the Return to service… and Rename… buttons are disabled unless ctx.admin, meaning the window was already elevated. The command runs without its own elevation prompt. The non-technical agent, following the sheet in an operator window, finds a disabled button and no prompt. The agent must first use Unlock settings…, which the checklist never mentions.
low.failure_scenario: The agent follows docs/10 at the laptop, signed in as an operator. Return to service… is greyed out and nothing in the checklist explains why.
low.suggested_fix: Add a step before step 3: 'Press Unlock settings… and enter the administrator password'. Move the password sentence there, and say the same in the Rename paragraph.

low.title: A late gap record for a run without footage starts the gap at a later run's footage
low.description: For a run with no segments, process_gap takes the gap start from `ledger.latest_recorded_segment(cam)` (db.py:854: newest row by rowid with end_utc). It does not limit this to segments recorded before that run. When the GapJob is processed late (a janitor retry after the first attempt failed, or startup recovery of a run whose gap was never written), a later run's sealed footage is chosen. `first_footage_after_run` then looks for footage after that wrong start. A janitor retry for an old run can also move an open gap's ended_run_id backwards in begin_gap (db.py:921-924).
low.failure_scenario: Run B (connect failure, no segments) ends. Its gap write fails ('database is locked' while the archive process is writing) and is not retried successfully before run C has sealed footage, for example because the service is restarted in between. When GapJob(B) is processed, the gap opens at the end of C's latest segment. C's next segment closes it as a bogus gap of about 0 s, and the real outage between the footage before B and C's start is missing from the ledger and from exports.
low.suggested_fix: Choose the start from segments of runs launched at or before the failed run, for example `... JOIN recording_runs r ... WHERE r.rowid <= (SELECT rowid FROM recording_runs WHERE run_id=?) ORDER BY r.rowid DESC, s.seq DESC LIMIT 1`. Likewise apply latest_gap_end only to gaps closed before that run's launch. In begin_gap, do not overwrite ended_run_id with an older run.

low.title: After an internal error, a segment file FFmpeg created but the loop had not registered yet is never registered, sealed or archived
low.description: The normal run end calls `_register_new_files` after FFmpeg exits (supervisor.py:573). `_abort_open_run` kills FFmpeg and seals only rows already in the ledger. It then marks the run ended, so startup recovery (which registers files only for unended runs or unknown folders) never looks at that folder again. No other code scans for unregistered seg_*.ts files.
low.failure_scenario: A ledger write raises in the recording loop (for example 'database is locked' in the 10 s last_stream_time_s update or in _on_closed) in the same iteration in which FFmpeg opened seg_N+1. FFmpeg is killed, the run is closed as internal_error, and seg_N+1 (the seconds written before the kill) stays on disk outside the ledger for good. It is never sealed or archived and never removed by retention, and its folder is never tidied.
low.suggested_fix: In `_abort_open_run`, after killing FFmpeg and before closing the books, call `self._register_new_files(run_id, self._open_run_dir, {})` (it skips paths already in the ledger), then continue with `_close_listed_segments` and the ACTIVE loop.

low.title: The 'recorder was not running' gap start uses events from other processes, so recorder downtime during a pause is labelled as the planned pause
low.description: `previous_instance_last_event` takes the newest row in the shared events table before the latest service_start as the previous recorder's last sign of life. The SentinelArchive service writes to the same table (category 'archive': drive attached, swap ready, copy errors and so on), and failed recorder starts (service_start/startup_failed loops) write there too. `_reconcile_gap_at_start` (supervisor.py:270-275) then ends the planned gap at that time and starts the 'recorder_not_running' gap only there.
low.failure_scenario: The recorder service is stopped, crashes, or loops on C-001 for 8 hours during a scheduled pause. Meanwhile the agent swaps the archive drive, and the archive process logs archive_swap_ready and archive_drive_attached events. When the recorder runs again, the gap says 'scheduled_pause' up to the last archive event and 'recorder_not_running' only for the last few minutes. The export presents unplanned downtime as a planned pause (the H3 problem class).
low.suggested_fix: Use only the recorder's own events: filter on `category IN ('recorder','schedule','motion','clock','recovery')` or `code != 'service_start'` from the recorder plus clock_observations, and exclude failed starts (a service_start immediately followed by startup_failed).

low.title: W-002 'Motion was detected but could not be recorded' is raised (CRITICAL) when a motion run is cut by the schedule switching to pause
low.description: For runs started in motion mode, a run that ended without video counts as a motion-recording failure unless the reason is GRACEFUL_STOP. A run ended by the schedule (SCHEDULED_PAUSE) while still connecting is counted too. The counter is reset only by a later run with video, so W-002 stays during the whole pause.
low.failure_scenario: Motion at 06:59:55 starts a run. At 07:00 the schedule switches to pause, the run stops after 5 s while still connecting, and motion_record_failures becomes 1. All through the pause the agent sees 'Recording stopped. Error W-002: Motion was detected but could not be recorded. Contact technical support...' (CRITICAL, with an automatic diagnostic report) next to P-001.
low.suggested_fix: Exclude planned ends: `elif for_motion and outcome.reason not in (RunEndReason.GRACEFUL_STOP, RunEndReason.SCHEDULED_PAUSE)`.

low.title: The content-hash worker fingerprints segments whose local original retention has already removed (or is removing)
low.description: hash_segment skips a segment only if content_sha256 is set or sha256 is None. It does not check local_deleted_utc, and it does not check it again before writing the sidecar and the ledger row. Only the start-up queue filters deleted segments (db.py:876). Retention runs in its own thread and does not wait for content hashing.
low.failure_scenario: With a content-hash backlog (see the timeout finding), retention removes an archived original that is still queued: FFmpeg fails, a 'content_hash_failed' warning is written and V-001 shows for 10 minutes. Or retention decides while the hash is running (the decision row records framehash_rel_path=NULL), and the worker then writes seg_X.framehash.txt. Retention never deletes that sidecar, and the ledger records a frame-hash path for a removed original.
low.suggested_fix: In hash_segment, return early if `seg['local_deleted_utc']`. Before the os.replace/update_segment step, read the row again and discard the result (and delete the .partial file) if local_deleted_utc has been set.

low.title: Keep-awake and the H-001 check may not cover laptops with Modern Standby (S0 low-power idle), where turning the screen off can put the PC into standby
low.description: The install sets the screen to turn off after 5 min (mains) or 2 min (battery), and the comment says recording continues. KeepAwake uses SetThreadExecutionState(ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED). On Modern Standby (S0ix) hardware, which many current rugged laptops use, standby is entered when the display turns off, and a system-required request may not prevent it; network can be cut in 'disconnected standby'. read_power_settings/sleep_risks look only at S3 idle timeouts and the lid action. They never check GetPwrCapabilities' AoAc flag, so H-001 would never warn. Not verified on hardware: flagged because the failure mode (recording stops a few minutes after the agent walks away) is the worst kind and checking it is cheap.
low.failure_scenario: On a Modern Standby rugged laptop, with no input for 5 minutes, the display turns off, the system enters Modern Standby, the camera connection drops, and the recorder stalls or retries. H-001 does not fire because the S3 standby timeouts read 'never'.
low.suggested_fix: Before deployment, run `powercfg /a` on the actual laptop. If 'Standby (S0 Low Power Idle)' is listed, also hold a PowerRequestExecutionRequired/SystemRequired power request via PowerCreateRequest/PowerSetRequest, and either disable display-off at install or verify with `powercfg /requests` and a 30-minute unattended test that recording continues with the screen off. Add an H-001 risk when the AoAc capability is present and screen-off is enabled.

low.title: Date-period edges in the autumn repeated hour are still evaluated with fold=0 only: P-001 says 'No time to resume recording is scheduled. Contact technical support'
low.description: The L22 fix made weekly edges produce both instants of a repeated wall-clock time (`_local_epochs`), but `_candidates` still converts date-period edges with `_local_epoch` (fold=0 only). state_at() compares the naive wall time against date bounds, so a date period that ends inside the repeated hour applies again during the second pass of that hour. Its second end instant is never a candidate.
low.failure_scenario: Europe/London, default record, [[schedule.dates]] pause 2026-10-20 00:00 to 2026-10-25 01:30. I checked with the venv: plan() gives pause until 00:30 UTC, record 00:30-01:00 UTC, then 'pause from 01:00 UTC, no change scheduled'. The real behaviour is pause 01:00-01:30 UTC, then record. During those 30 minutes next_change() returns None, so the operator's P-001 reads 'No time to resume recording is scheduled. Contact technical support if recording should be running.', and the technician's plan shows a permanent pause. (A date edge in the spring gap is also only right when the DST switch is within 9 days of now or of a date end, so far-ahead plans can be off by the gap length.)
low.suggested_fix: In _candidates use `for t in self._local_epochs(edge)` for date-period edges, as for weekly bounds, and add each end instant as a base. Also scan offset changes around every date edge, not only within 9 days of the bases.

low.title: P-001 says 'Recording resumes automatically on X' when the next scheduled change is to motion-only recording
low.description: pause_message() always says recording resumes at resume_epoch. resume_epoch is next_change() from a pause, which may be a change to 'motion' (for example pause at weekends, default = motion). At that time the recorder only starts watching for motion (P-003). status.json next_change_is already reports 'motion' correctly, but the operator text does not.
low.failure_scenario: default = "motion", weekly record weekdays 07:00-19:00, weekly pause Sat-Sun. On Sunday the agent reads 'Recording resumes automatically on Mon 00:00. No action is needed.' From Monday 00:00 to 07:00 nothing is recorded unless motion is detected, which contradicts what the agent was told.
low.suggested_fix: Pass schedule.mode_at(resume_epoch) into pause_message and say 'Motion-triggered recording starts on X' (or 'Recording resumes on X') to match it.

low.title: Preview reader has no stall watchdog: a preview FFmpeg that stays connected but emits no frames keeps the camera session after the viewer leaves
low.description: The viewer-gone check runs only after `proc.stdout.read1()` returns data. If FFmpeg keeps receiving packets (so the RTSP -timeout never fires) but produces no JPEG output (undecodable stream, decoder stuck on a damaged GOP), read1 blocks indefinitely. The preview then never notices the request has expired and keeps the camera connection and decoder running until the service stops. The motion detector got a watchdog for exactly this in the 2026-11-10 review (L24); the preview, added the same day, did not.
low.failure_scenario: After a camera firmware hiccup the main stream delivers packets the decoder rejects. The preview FFmpeg stays alive with no output. The agent closes the window, but the extra RTSP session and decode stay up for days, and the state stays 'live' with an old frame.
low.suggested_fix: Add the same watchdog as MotionDetector._run_ffmpeg: a thread that kills the preview FFmpeg when no frame has been published for ~20-30 s or when request_is_fresh() turns false, independent of the blocking read.

low.title: Verifier reads ledger_chain_pending once at start; a protection gap that arises during the check is reported as alteration (V-003)
low.description: self.pending is loaded in the first snapshot. key_pass and unlogged_pass run later, in other snapshots, and use it to decide between a 'not_yet_protected' fault (V-004) and a 'record_altered' or 'record_unlogged' finding (V-003). If a chain entry fails after the check started, the recorder commits the row change together with a pending marker in one transaction. The later snapshot then shows the changed row, but the pending marker is not in self.pending, so the check reports alteration.
low.failure_scenario: The hourly integrity-worker verify is running. The audit then updates audit_status on segment S, and the chain insert fails, for example with 'database or disk is full' inside the savepoint; the row and its pending marker are committed. check_key(S) sees the row differ from the latest entry with no pending marker and adds 'record_altered'. V-003 'The recording log has been altered' is raised and a permanent 'ledger_chain_altered' error event is written, for what is only a V-004 protection gap.
low.suggested_fix: Read ledger_chain_pending for the key (or the batch of keys) inside the same snapshot as the row comparison in check_key and unlogged_pass, rather than relying on the start-of-check copy.

low.title: ledger verify: an exception exits with status 1 ('altered'), and a non-elevated run says the database 'was not found'
low.description: main() documents exit codes 0 intact, 1 altered, 2 cannot check, 3 gaps. Errors from verify_ledger, anchors_from, or the file hashing in check_files (sqlite3 errors after the 5 s transient retry, 'database disk image is malformed', PermissionError or sharing violation on a spool file) are not caught, so Python prints a traceback and exits with status 1, the 'altered' code. Separately, `db.exists()` returns False when a non-elevated prompt cannot see into the service-only data folder (Path.exists swallows the access error), so the user is told 'The recording database was not found; nothing to check.' docs/09 steps 5.5 and 7.3 tell the operator to run `Sentinel.exe ledger head` and `verify` without saying 'as administrator'.
low.failure_scenario: A technician follows docs/09 step 7.3 from a normal Command Prompt and reads that the recording database was not found, which looks like data loss. Or a verify run as administrator while the recorder restarts hits a transient error longer than 5 s; the traceback exits 1, which a checklist or script reads as 'altered'.
low.suggested_fix: Wrap the verify/head body in try/except Exception, print a plain 'cannot check: <reason>' and return 2. Before the exists() check, test os.access on the data folder (or catch PermissionError from os.stat) and say 'run as administrator'. Add 'as administrator' to docs/09 steps 5.5 and 7.3.

low.title: After a broken entry, every saved fingerprint is also reported as 'entries were removed from the end'; protection-gap text always says the changes were legitimate
low.description: When chain_pass stops at the first broken or altered entry k, `expected` is k. The log_truncated loop then adds one finding for each anchor with seq >= k: 'The log ends at entry k-1 … entries were removed from the end'. That can be thousands of lines, since an anchor is written every 15 minutes, and it misstates what happened (an edit, not a truncation). Separately, the protection_gap fault message (line 1064-1067) always says 'Only changes the recording software would make were found across the gap', even when check_key reports an illegal_change across that same gap.
low.failure_scenario: One event row's chain record is edited. The report correctly names entry k as the first problem, but 'All problems' then lists hundreds of 'entries were removed from the end' lines. An examiner reading the list concludes that the log was cut back, which it was not.
low.suggested_fix: Only emit log_truncated when the chain verified cleanly to its end (not self.broken). Otherwise add one note that later fingerprints could not be compared because of the break. Make the protection-gap message neutral, or say what the rule check across the gap found.

low.title: acknowledge() reports already-acknowledged or non-existent problem ids as acknowledged
low.description: acknowledge(admin_id, problem_ids) returns len(ids) and writes an audit event listing all ids. Ids that do not exist or were already acknowledged are included, because the UPDATE (guarded by `acknowledged_utc IS NULL`) changes nothing for them and nothing checks the row count. The CLI prints 'N archive problem(s) acknowledged', and the chained audit event records an acknowledgement that did not happen.
low.failure_scenario: An administrator types `archive acknowledge --problem 12` with a mistyped id, or an id another admin already acknowledged. The output is '1 archive problem(s) acknowledged' and the A-006 alert stays up, which confuses the agent. The ledger's audit event also lists problem 12 as acknowledged by this admin.
low.suggested_fix: Count cursor.rowcount per UPDATE and return and record only the ids actually changed. Report unknown or already-acknowledged ids separately.

low.title: The drive declared safe to remove is forgotten when the volume list cannot be read, and is written again if it is still inserted
low.description: _select debounces the swapped drive over two scans but ignores scan.uncertain. When FindFirstVolumeW fails, the scan returns no candidates and uncertain is set, so _swapped_absent_polls reaches 2 and _set_swapped(None) deletes swapped_drive.json. When enumeration works again and the drive is still in the port (the agent has not unplugged it yet), it is just a usable archive drive, so it is attached and copying resumes on it. The attached drive gets a 10-scan allowance under uncertain (UNCERTAIN_MISSES); the swapped drive gets none.
low.failure_scenario: After a swap (REMOVE_MANUALLY), the volume enumeration fails for about 10 s (driver hiccup). The swapped drive is forgotten, then re-attached and written to while the screen had told the agent to take it out. The agent pulls it mid-copy: A-003, a .partial is left, and an unclean NTFS unplug.
low.suggested_fix: In _select, do not increment _swapped_absent_polls while scan.uncertain is set (treat it as swapped_present, as is done for scan.unusable).

low.title: A refused archive drive or a folder in the operator request folder writes a chained warning event on every poll, forever
low.description: _take_operator leaves a directory or junction named swap.request or resume.request in place (correctly) but logs the archive_*_request_ignored event every time it looks. That is twice per step (every poll_interval_s = 5 s) plus every second during a copy (_poll_swap_in_flight). Any standard user in the operators group can create such a folder. Likewise, _refuse (line 500) records archive_drive_unusable on every step while a refused drive stays inserted: a write test denied by the drive ACL, a review layout, or the same volume. Each event is a hash-chained ledger row.
low.failure_scenario: An operator (or a tool) creates the folder <status_dir>\requests\swap.request. The ledger gains about 17,000 to 86,000 chained warning events per day for the whole deployment, which bloats sentinel.db and the event views and buries real events.
low.suggested_fix: Rate-limit these events: log once per distinct (kind, why) or drive identity until the condition changes. In _take_operator, remember that the ignored object is a folder (by inode or mtime) and stay silent until it changes. In _refuse, record the event only on the first refusal of a given drive_key/reason.

low.title: Operator messages tell the agent to wait for SAFE TO REMOVE (never shown in this build) and not to use Safely Remove even with separate USB drives
low.description: Only ManualRemovalFallback is shipped (ejected is always False), so state SAFE_TO_REMOVE never occurs. Yet MSG_FULL (line 107) and the window's swap note say "wait for SAFE TO REMOVE". With another drive present, _removal_text says "Do not use Windows' Safely Remove Hardware for it: in a two-bay dock that would also stop the other drive". docs (commit c8c3157) now recommend separate external USB drives, where Safely Remove is exactly what the agent should use, and where pulling without it is the A-003-style unplug the docs warn against.
low.failure_scenario: An agent with two separate USB SSDs presses Swap and waits for "SAFE TO REMOVE", which never appears. The status meanwhile says not to use Safely Remove Hardware, so the agent either waits indefinitely or pulls the drive without the OS safe-removal.
low.suggested_fix: Word MSG_FULL and the window note as "wait until this page says the drive can be taken out". Show the dock-specific sentence only when both drives are known to be in one multi-bay enclosure (or drop it), and otherwise tell the agent to use Safely Remove Hardware for that drive.

low.title: Safely remove ignores the archive copier and trusts the drive number from an old listing; with two drives whose serials are hidden, its 'is it gone' check never passes
low.description: (1) cmd_eject and safe_remove have no idea which drive is the archive drive in use. The window offers 'Safely remove…' for any drive, including the one being copied to. CM_Request_Device_EjectW succeeds between two files, and the copier then finds its drive gone without a swap: A-003, and no index or playlists written. docs/10 step 1 says such a drive must go back to the laptop and be swapped first. When the veto does happen, the message 'Close any open files on it' cannot be acted on, because the open files are the copier's. (2) The window passes only --disk <n> from the listing it last read, and nothing checks the disk's identity, so a renumbered disk gets ejected. (3) verify_gone tests `same_device` (serial, unique_id, model, size, bus). If another connected disk has the same hardware key (two identical drives whose serials are hidden), the ejected drive never looks gone, and after 15 s the agent is told 'The drive did not disconnect. Do not unplug it. Contact technical support.' even though Windows ejected it.
low.failure_scenario: The agent selects 'archive drive SSD_1 — In use' and presses Safely remove instead of Swap. The eject succeeds between two segments, the window says SAFE TO REMOVE, and the agent takes it to the office. The copier records an unexpected removal, and the drive's index does not list the latest files, so the office check fails or misses recordings.
low.suggested_fix: In cmd_eject, read the archive status or the drive's marker role. For the drive the copier is using, refuse and tell the agent to use Swap archive drive. Pass the fingerprint from the window and refuse if the disk changed. In verify_gone, check that the disk's pnp_device_id (or full fingerprint) is gone, not its hardware key.

low.title: A connected drive's volume label can crash the choice of the next drive name (str.isdigit accepts digits int() rejects)
low.description: _label_number uses `label[len(prefix):].isdigit()` and then calls int(). isdigit() is True for superscript digits and other Unicode digits such as '²' and '①', which int() rejects. next_label() reads the labels of every connected volume and of every record, so one foreign drive labelled 'SSD_²' makes prepare_drive raise ValueError, which the command line does not catch. The probe confirmed the error: "invalid literal for int() with base 10: '²'".
low.failure_scenario: A USB stick labelled 'SSD_²' is connected while the agent sets up a new SSD. Erase and set up fails with a traceback, and keeps failing until the stick is removed. Nothing explains why.
low.suggested_fix: Use `s.isascii() and s.isdecimal()`, or a regex `\d+` with re.ASCII, and wrap the int() call.

low.title: A drive with a UniqueId but no serial is offered for erasing, but can never be confirmed from the window or with --yes
low.description: A drive with a UniqueId but no serial passes has_hardware_identity, so classification offers erasing (can_prepare=True). In the --yes path, cmd_prepare requires `typed == confirm_text(serial)`. confirm_text(None) is None (and so is a serial with fewer than serial_confirm_chars letters and digits), so every --serial-tail is refused with 'The confirmation given does not match this drive.' The window's EraseDialog asks for 'last 4 characters of the serial number', but the list shows an empty serial.
low.failure_scenario: An SSD in a bridge that reports a UniqueId but no serial shows as blank and erasable. The agent cannot type any accepted value, and keeps getting 'does not match this drive', which suggests the wrong drive was picked.
low.suggested_fix: Make classification refuse such drives (reason no_identity, with a clear message), or define a confirmation word for them, as with hidden serials (HIDDEN_SERIAL_WORD), and apply it the same way in the window, cmd_prepare and check_guards.

low.title: The placeholder-serial check misses common bridge filler serials; the drives table's serial-only match then marks every new disk in such an enclosure as holding recordings
low.description: serial_is_placeholder catches only one repeated character, an ascending run starting at 0 or 1, or a filler word. Verified as NOT a placeholder: '1234567890', '123456789012', '00000000000000000001', and the JMicron default 'DB9876543214E' (a descending run). For such serials known.matches falls through to the hardware match. Its `disk.serial.lower() in self.serials` branch uses the drives table's serial column alone, without model or size; export/ledger.upsert_drive stores the bridge's serial there (C2). Every new disk later put in the same model of enclosure then counts as known_hardware, shows as SENTINEL_EVIDENCE ('Sentinel's records show it set up a drive with this serial number before'), and can never be set up. confirm_text also asks for the tail of a serial that is not printed on the drive's label.
low.failure_scenario: The archive drive in a JMicron enclosure that reports 'DB9876543214E' is exported to or designated once. A brand-new SSD put in an identical enclosure is refused as 'holds Sentinel recordings' forever, and the agent is left stuck with 'Contact technical support'.
low.suggested_fix: Extend the placeholder check: descending runs, runs that wrap around ('1234567890', '123456789012'), long strings of zeros with a few trailing digits, and known bridge defaults. In KnownDrives, match a serial from the drives table only together with model and size, as is already done for drive_prepared records.

low.title: A resumed or retried export finishes its old, frozen interval and reports 'Export complete' without saying newer recordings are missing
low.description: resumable_batch returns any non-terminal batch for the drive, however old, or the last FAILED one. The engine completes that batch's plan from when it was made and tells the operator 'SAFE TO REMOVE DRIVE. Export complete and verified.' (or the manual-removal text). The message never says that recordings made after that plan are not included and that Export must be pressed again.
low.failure_scenario: On Monday the drive is pulled mid-export (E-002 tells the agent to insert the same drive and press again). The agent comes back on Friday and presses Export with the same drive. Monday's batch completes and the agent is told it is complete. The drive goes to the reviewer without Tuesday to Friday, although it had room for them.
low.suggested_fix: When a resumed or retried batch completes and newer sealed footage exists, say so in the final status and result message ('This drive holds recordings up to <time>. Press Export again to add newer recordings.'), or chain a second batch automatically.

low.title: Summary page says every MP4 was checked frame by frame, but the default level is 'sampled'
low.description: The static text in Export_Summary.html says 'the MP4 pictures were checked frame by frame against the originals', whatever the level actually used. [export] content_check defaults to 'sampled' (config.py:133), and 'deferred' does no picture check at all. The same page's table shows 'sample of frames checked' or 'pictures not yet checked', so this reviewer-facing document contradicts itself.
low.failure_scenario: Any export with the default config: a reviewer or court reads in the summary that every frame was compared, which was not done.
low.suggested_fix: Make the sentence depend on the levels present, for example 'MP4 pictures were compared with the originals as shown in the column "Pictures compared with originals"', or state per level.

low.title: Retention can delete a source during a running export, which fails with critical E-006 (only the next run plans again)
low.description: The M3 fix (removed_sources / _replan) runs only when a batch is resumed. RetentionManager._eligible still ignores export_items of active batches, so a segment can be removed from the spool while an export is copying. _copy_file / _copy_mp4 then raise SourceReadError or 'local recording missing', which becomes E-006 'A recording on this system could not be read for export. Contact technical support', with an export_failed error event that reads like evidence loss. The next press plans again and succeeds.
low.failure_scenario: An export of a large backlog on a nearly full SSD, with retention enabled and the archive drive removed. Retention runs every 60 s and removes a not-yet-copied segment of the running batch, and the agent gets a critical E-006 alert.
low.suggested_fix: Have retention skip segments that a non-terminal (or last FAILED) export batch still needs, or have the engine check local_deleted_utc when a source read fails and plan again or mark it 'kept only on archive drives' instead of raising E-006.

low.title: After a replan, files the abandoned batch had already verified stay on the drive but are not in any manifest
low.description: The _replan docstring says files already verified on the drive 'are kept and re-checked by the new batch'. That holds only when the new plan has an item with the same path. When a removed segment splits an MP4 group, the new group gets a different name, because names hold the start and end times. The old MP4, which also contains the removed segment's footage, and that segment's original stay on the drive (read-only and verified) but are in no manifest or SHA256SUMS.txt of that drive.
low.failure_scenario: Batch 1 verifies Recordings/.../100000-110000_*.mp4 from segments 1-12, then the drive is pulled. Retention removes segment 11 and the new plan makes 100000-105000 and 105500-110000. The reviewer sees three overlapping videos, and one of them is not listed in the summary or the hash list.
low.suggested_fix: When planning again, list the verified items of the abandoned batch that the new plan does not include (carry them as already_present items, or as 'from an earlier unfinished export' entries with their recorded SHA-256) so every file on the drive is in a manifest.

low.title: verify-content on a drive with no Sentinel exports says 'All videos on this drive have already been checked'
low.description: _verify_content treats an empty deferred_mp4s(drive_key) as success. A wrong drive gives the same reassuring answer: a fresh stick, an archive drive, or a review drive whose key changed (for example after a marker was added).
low.failure_scenario: The agent picks the wrong letter in the Export page and presses 'Check the video on the drive'. They are told every video was checked picture by picture, though the drive has no exports at all.
low.suggested_fix: Tell the cases apart. If no COMPLETE review batch exists for this drive_key, return 'This drive holds no Sentinel review export' (FAILED or a distinct state) instead of the 'already checked' message.

low.title: A verification mismatch (E-003) becomes a permanent 'different files with the same names' (E-004) on retry
low.description: When the read-back of a file Sentinel itself wrote does not match, the item becomes FAILED and the final file stays on the drive. On retry, reset_failed_items makes the item PLANNED, _copy_phase_item finds the file and calls _existing, and _conflict raises E-004. It does this on every retry, with a message implying someone else's files are in the way.
low.failure_scenario: A marginal drive corrupts one original. The first attempt reports E-003. Every later attempt reports E-004 'The review drive already holds different files with the same names', and the drive can never finish its export.
low.suggested_fix: Note in the item's error or detail that the file was written by this batch. On retry, move it to a quarantine name or explain it as 'a file written earlier did not verify (drive fault)'. Keep the E-003 wording and advise using another drive.

low.title: docs/05 says closing the window has no effect on an export because the export runs in the service; it runs as a child of the window
low.description: Row 21 says 'Operator closes GUI during recording / export: No effect ... Phase 3 export runs in the service'. The Export page actually starts 'Sentinel export run' through its command panel (gui/app/drive_pages.py:611), and the window asks before stopping a running command, so closing the window can kill an export. A kill between a rename and the ledger update can also cause the E-007 loop described above.
low.failure_scenario: A technician relies on this table and tells the agent closing the window is harmless during an export. The export is killed and left half-finished.
low.suggested_fix: Correct the row: the export runs as a child process of the window, closing the window asks and then stops it, and the next press resumes the batch on the same drive.

low.title: Status and Drives pages show values from an outdated status file as current, and enable Swap from it
low.description: viewmodel.build_dashboard says alerts in a stale document must not be shown and shows camera 'Unknown'. Its consumers ignore read.kind, though. StatusPage.on_status (status_pages.py:282-286) lists the stale document's alerts next to X-001. _header/_facts (status_pages.py:324-328, 374-375, 389-410) show 'Camera: connected' and 'Clock synchronised: yes' in green, plus the archive message. DrivesPage.on_status sets _arc_running and the Cancel-swap visibility from the stale archive section, and shows its message (e.g. 'Copying… do not unplug' or 'SAFE TO REMOVE') with no hint that it is old. The archive section comes from the recorder, so it freezes whenever the recorder is down, even when the archive copier is still running.
low.failure_scenario: The recorder service crashes (X-001), but the archive copier keeps running. The Drives page keeps showing the archive state from before the crash, and Swap stays enabled. An operator requests a swap through the request folder. The copier makes the drive safe, but the page never shows SAFE TO REMOVE, so the agent either waits indefinitely or unplugs based on an old message. The Status page shows the camera as connected in green under 'System error'.
low.suggested_fix: When read.kind is not OK, show the per-field facts as 'unknown / last known at HH:MM' in a neutral tone, list only X-001 (and Z-001), and on the Drives page say that the archive state is not current. Do not base Swap enablement on a stale 'running' flag.

low.title: Live view keeps the recorder decoding the camera's main stream all the time while the window sits minimised or locked on the Status page
low.description: LiveView stops only on Page.on_hide, which runs when another page is chosen. Minimising the window, locking Windows (lock_computer() just minimises) or covering it does not stop the 0.5 s timer, which renews preview.request every 5 s. While that file is fresh, the recorder service runs an extra FFmpeg on the camera's MAIN stream and writes 1920-wide JPEGs five times a second (preview.py docstring). Status is the default and remembered page, and the window is typically left open on the site laptop.
low.failure_scenario: The agent leaves Sentinel open on Status and locks the computer. For days, the service keeps a third RTSP session open to the camera (recorder, motion detector, preview), decodes the full-resolution stream and writes JPEGs about five times a second to the SSD. This uses CPU and disk on the rugged laptop and can hit the camera's session limit, which then shows up as recorder connection failures.
low.suggested_fix: In _tick, skip the request (and stop the timer) when self.window().isMinimized() or the widget is not visible, or when the application state is not active. Restart it on showEvent or on application activation.

low.title: A status document with a wrongly typed field raises inside refresh() and freezes the whole window display at the last good state
low.description: read_status_robust only catches malformed documents whose root is not a dict. build_dashboard and the window/pages call .get() on nested values without checking their type: alerts entries (line 345), 'alert' (346), 'open_gap' (401), 'storage'/'archive' (window.py:444-447, drive_pages.py:293/299, status_pages.py:338-352) and alert 'detail' (status_pages.py:300). I checked with the venv: {'alerts': ['x']}, {'storage': 'x'}, {'alert': 'R-001'} and {'open_gap': 'x'} all raise AttributeError in build_dashboard. The exception leaves AppWindow.refresh() before _show_summary, so every 3-second refresh fails silently (in a windowed build stderr is None). The state label, status bar and Status page keep showing the previous values, for example 'Recording normally'.
low.failure_scenario: A status.json written by another version after an update or rollback, or by a partly broken writer, contains 'storage': null-like text or an alert that is a plain string. The window keeps showing the last good 'Recording normally' with a frozen 'Updated' time, with no X-001.
low.suggested_fix: Normalise the document once in read_status_robust: coerce non-dict sections to {} and drop non-dict alerts. Alternatively, wrap refresh() so that any exception is shown as X-001/'status unreadable' instead of leaving the old display.

low.title: Operator-enabled 'Archive details' and 'Archive problems' read the service-only data folder: they report wrong results or fail with a traceback
low.description: arc_status_btn and problems_btn are not limited to administrators. 'archive status' reads cfg.data_path/archive_status.json. 'acknowledge' (the listing) opens Ledger(data_path/sentinel.db). After the service install, the data folder is readable only by SYSTEM, Administrators and the service. For an operator, read_archive_status() returns None and the command prints 'Archive copying has not run yet.' even while copying runs. The problems listing raises an uncaught sqlite3/permission error and shows 'failed (exit code 1)' with a traceback.
low.failure_scenario: An operator presses 'Archive details' to check the copy before a swap and is told archive copying has never run, which looks like an archiving failure. They press 'Archive problems' and see a Python traceback.
low.suggested_fix: For non-administrators, either disable these two buttons with a tooltip, or show the archive section from status.json, which operators can read.

low.title: GUI ledger reads on the UI thread use the default 5-second retry, so the window can freeze repeatedly
low.description: open_ledger() constructs Ledger(db_path, readonly=True) without retry_seconds. Ledger defaults to READ_RETRY_SECONDS = 5 and retries 'unable to open database file', 'database is locked' and 'disk i/o error' with sleeps, both on connect and on each query (db.py:463-475). db.py's own docstring says a UI thread must pass 0. snapshot() runs on the UI thread every 3 s (connect plus three queries). The Recordings, System and Export pages call load_* on the UI thread as well.
low.failure_scenario: An account that is not in 'Sentinel Operators' can see that the snapshot exists but cannot open it, or the disk returns I/O errors. Each 3-second refresh blocks the UI for at least 5 s and up to about 20 s, so the window is shown as 'Not responding' and cannot even be used to save a diagnostic report.
low.suggested_fix: Pass retry_seconds=0 in open_ledger (treat a failure as 'temporarily unavailable'), or move snapshot/timeline loading to a Task.

low.title: Any background task (e.g. saving a diagnostic report) is labelled 'starting the recorder': closing is refused and updates are blocked with a wrong reason
low.description: busy_work() reports every running Task in self._tasks as 'starting the recorder', but save_report() also adds its Task to _tasks (line 511). closeEvent then refuses to close with 'Wait until the recorder has been restarted… Closing now would leave it stopped'. UpdatesTab._ready() refuses with 'Wait until this has finished first: starting the recorder'. _tasks is also never pruned.
low.failure_scenario: The agent saves a diagnostic report (an integrity check and chain verify can take a while) and then tries to close the window or apply an update. They are told the recorder is being restarted, which is false and alarming.
low.suggested_fix: Keep the setup-start task separately (or tag each task with a description), and name each running task correctly in busy_work. Remove finished tasks from _tasks.

low.title: The archive service runs without the program-file write check that the recorder service enforces
low.description: run_recorder_in_host refuses to start when code_write_problems finds that the program folder, the config or FFmpeg can be changed by non-administrators. run_archive_in_host has no such check, although it runs the same SentinelService.exe and its service SID has Modify on the data folder, which holds the hash-chained ledger.
low.failure_scenario: The program folder becomes writable by Users (for example copied outside Program Files, or an ACL changed). The recorder refuses with C-001, but SentinelArchive keeps running possibly-replaced code with write access to sentinel.db and archive status.
low.suggested_fix: Run the same code_check in run_archive_in_host before creating the worker, and report through event_log (and A- status) when it fails.

low.title: winsvc status gives a non-existent command for exit 2 and does not report the SentinelArchive service
low.description: EXIT_MEANINGS[2] tells the technician to 'run: python -m sentinel.service check-config'. The deployed build has no Python; the equivalent is 'Sentinel.exe check-config'. cmd_host's NotStartedByScm text also says 'python -m sentinel.service run'. cmd_status queries only SentinelRecorder, so a crash-looping or stopped SentinelArchive still gives an OK result. Bench step 1.9 relies on this command.
low.failure_scenario: A technician follows the hint printed for a stopped recorder ('python' is not recognised). Separately, 'Check service' says healthy while the archive copier is stopped, and the backlog only appears later as A-007.
low.suggested_fix: Use Sentinel.exe wording when frozen (as service.py:206-208 already does). Also query ARCHIVE_SERVICE_NAME in cmd_status (when [archive] is enabled) and count it in 'healthy'.

low.title: set-camera silently turns an rtsps camera into rtsp
low.description: current_address accepts any URL starting with 'rtsp', rtsps included, but set_camera always rebuilds the URL as 'rtsp://host:port/path'. The scheme is not kept. The old review fixed the same problem in the window ('rtsps cameras stay rtsps'), but not in the CLI.
low.failure_scenario: The camera uses rtsps://cam:322/stream. A technician runs 'Sentinel.exe set-camera' to change the password. The URL is rewritten to rtsp://cam:322/stream. The recorder then either fails to connect (an R- outage), or, if the camera also accepts plain RTSP, sends the camera credentials without TLS.
low.suggested_fix: Keep the existing scheme: take it from the current URL (default rtsp) and build f"{scheme}://...".

low.title: Return to service and Rename are refused with a misleading message when the archive SSD picks up any soft 'unsuitable' reason
low.description: _return() and _rename() require class == 'READY'. classify() returns READY only when _unsuitable_reasons() is empty (classify.py:245-246). Otherwise a drive with a marker becomes SENTINEL_EVIDENCE. Soft reasons that can appear on a deployed archive SSD include: SMART 'Warning' (health), the administrator raising 'Smallest drive accepted' above the SSD's size (too_small), and a transient ledger read error (ledger_unavailable). Return then says 'Select the archive drive that came back from the office (it shows as "archive drive SSD_…")', although the row does show 'archive drive SSD_1 — holds Sentinel recordings (never erased)'. Rename says the drive was not set up by Sentinel and suggests Erase and set up, which is refused.
low.failure_scenario: An administrator sets 'Smallest drive accepted' to 2000 GB to block small drives. The existing 1.9 TB SSD_1 comes back from the office, and Return to service tells the agent to select the archive drive, which they did. Nothing tells them why, so the drive cannot be put back into service.
low.suggested_fix: Gate Return and Rename on a valid marker with role 'archive' (or any valid marker for Rename), not on the erase classification. Show the actual reason when refusing.

low.title: A heartbeat written before a backward clock correction counts as fresh for hours, hiding a dead recorder or copier
low.description: read_status computes age = time.time() - heartbeat_epoch and flags only age > max_age_s. copier_running (archive/status.py:141), RecorderArchiveView.evaluate (archive/status.py:201-202) and archive_alive (launcher/control.py:98-99) do the same. A heartbeat from the future (negative age) is always treated as fresh.
low.failure_scenario: The laptop clock is 5 h fast. The recorder (or archive copier) hangs or is killed, leaving a heartbeat stamped at the wrong time. Time sync then corrects the clock back by 5 h. For up to 5 hours the window shows 'Recording normally' (no X-001), or the archive as running (no A-007), from the stale file. Swap and Return also believe the copier is running and wait.
low.suggested_fix: Treat heartbeat_epoch more than a small tolerance (e.g. 2 x the status interval) in the future as suspicious. Count staleness from the last time the reader saw the heartbeat value change (monotonic clock in the reader), or include a monotonic sequence number in the status file.

coverage.covered: Read end to end: src/sentinel/recorder/supervisor.py, finalizer.py, recovery.py, integrity.py, timebase.py, segment_list.py, ffmpeg_cmd.py and progress.py; service.py, status.py, alerts.py, watchdog.py, selfcheck.py and power.py. Followed calls into db.py (tx/lock, runs, segments, seal, begin_gap, switch_open_gap, close_gap, previous_instance_last_event), the ledgerchain covered columns and illegal_changes for runs, gaps and segments, storage/monitor.py, media/probe.py, platform/windows.py (bind_child, fsync), the winsvc run_recorder_in_host exit path, and the GUI watch/rollback in window.py. Ran throwaway scripts with the venv: R-005 with since_seal=None (confirmed ERROR R-005); _read_progress with a freeze plus burst catch-up (confirmed drift never confirmed or cleared); real Ledger plus Finalizer for the janitor gap retry (confirmed a gap with negative duration and clock_anomaly, and the open gap lost). No repo files were changed. I noticed an untracked docs/REVIEW-2026-11-12.md from an earlier run tonight: the R-005, selfcheck and R-004 items overlap it (marked in the descriptions); the other findings are not in it. Not checked in depth: the motion detector internals, schedule.py edge cases, the archive/retention internals, and real FFmpeg behaviour (the burst-after-freeze timing is modelled, not captured from a real camera).

Read in full: src/sentinel/schedule.py, clock.py, ledger_timing.py, timesync.py, motion.py, preview.py, media/probe.py, media/videohash.py, recorder/timebase.py, recorder/progress.py, recorder/ffmpeg_cmd.py, and the sim/camera.py header (sim is not imported by production code). Followed the calls into recorder/supervisor.py (schedule pause, motion standby, run loop, drift knots, _end_run, _read_progress), recorder/finalizer.py _corrections/_timestamps, recorder/recovery.py crash close, service.py (detector, preview and schedule wiring, _check_clock, clock observations, status/P-001), gui/app/liveview.py, status_pages.py and the window's page switching, config.py schedule loading, and the archive __main__ config load. Read docs/03 §4 and docs/branches/motion-recording.md.

Throwaway scripts in the scratchpad (nothing in the repo was changed):
- s1: a date edge in the autumn repeated hour, plus timing of a large schedule (next_change 10 ms, 14-day plan 0.22 s; fine).
- s2: brute-force next_change against minute-by-minute evaluation in America/New_York, Europe/London, Australia/Lord_Howe, America/Santiago and America/Havana for weekly, overnight, Sunday-24:00 and date schedules. Only the date-fold case failed.
- s3: the date-dependent 'never records' refusal.
- m1: MotionAnalyzer cost (about 1 ms per frame, fine) and the duplicate-frame behaviour.
